domains.title: Linux kernel programming and lifetime boundaries
domains.depth: derivation, implementation, falsification and delayed transfer

subtopics.title: Failure-safe module initialization

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Show each owned bit has exactly one release and no release precedes its dependents. Relate O(3) model work to the number of real acquisitions, including a failure before endpoint publication.

Implement and investigate: Implement kl_unwind for an ownership mask whose bits0,1,2 mean buffer, workqueue and registered endpoint. Return the decimal release trace with resource numbers3,2,1 in reverse order; unknown bits return0. Derive the acquire/fail matrix, then apply it to the supplied teaching module init labels.

Falsify and transfer: Repair forward-order cleanup and double release on a second failure label; a module that returns ENOMEM after leaking work is incorrect even if loading fails. Then Replace one acquisition by a managed device allocation and demonstrate which cleanup obligations migrate to the device lifecycle, including failure after publication.

subtopics.title: User-copy progress and ABI admission

objectives.text: Derive and defend: State ownership of unread input, modified prefix and untouched suffix. Explain why a partial-copy return cannot be reused as a negative errno and why cap admission precedes copying.

Implement and investigate: Implement kl_copy into a live disjoint destination with capacity cap. Reject n>cap with -1 before writes; otherwise copy min(n,fault_after) bytes and return the completed count. The model input is ordinary accessible memory; a separate guest adapter must use copy_from_user and preserve its actual return convention.

Falsify and transfer: A faulty wrapper returns the requested count after a partial copy and exposes stale bytes. Demonstrate the stale sentinel in the original local teaching endpoint without touching other processes. Then Change the ABI to all-or-nothing record publication using private staging; inject a fault after a valid header and show no record becomes visible.

subtopics.title: Reference acquisition before handoff

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Associate every reference with a named owner; count conservation is initial plus successful acquires minus releases. Explain why a nonzero count cannot validate a pointer that may already be freed.

Implement and investigate: Implement kl_ref with op0 acquire and op1 release for a live KLRef initialized to {1,0}. Reject unknown operations, zero/dead acquisition and UINT_MAX overflow; reject repeated release. Last release sets dead exactly once. Failed transitions preserve the struct. Map each transition to kref_init/get/put and protected lookup in the VM adapter.

Falsify and transfer: Reject resurrection after the terminal release and a get-after-handoff schedule. Delaying free alone masks the race without creating valid ownership. Then Add a lookup table and compare mutex-protected get-unless-zero with RCU-protected storage lifetime; show why refcount and grace period solve different obligations.

subtopics.title: Context-sensitive locking

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive preemption, migration, interrupt and inter-CPU exclusion separately. A lockdep trace is evidence for exercised lock-order paths, not a proof of all schedules.

Implement and investigate: Implement kl_lock_allowed(context,kind,rt) for conservative teaching policy: context0 task,1 hardirq,2 softirq; kind0 mutex,1 spinlock_t,2 raw_spinlock_t. Mutex is task-only; raw lock is allowed in all three; ordinary spin lock is allowed in all non-RT contexts and only task context in this restricted RT exercise. Reject out-of-range fields. Defend why the policy is deliberately narrower than all Linux APIs.

Falsify and transfer: Repair an RT hardirq path that uses ordinary spinlock_t and a second-core race hidden by local interrupt disabling. The host truth table assesses policy only. Then Move a callback from task context to threaded IRQ and then hardirq; revise allocation and lock choices and retain the failed and corrected guest traces.

subtopics.title: Work cancellation and terminal ownership

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Prove release implies quiescence and closed admission. Compare cancellation return values with work ownership; do not hold a lock required by the worker while synchronously draining it.

Implement and investigate: Implement kl_work for serialized state {queued,running,closed,released}. Events0 submit,1 begin,2 complete,3 close,4 release. Admission fails when closed or occupied; begin transfers queued to running; complete requires running; close is idempotent; release succeeds only once when closed and neither queued nor running. Rejected events preserve state.

Falsify and transfer: A faulty release ignores running work after close; the sentinel release flag demonstrates premature destruction. A deadlock also occurs if teardown waits while holding the worker lock. Then Allow a worker to requeue itself; introduce a closure generation and prove no requeue survives the close linearization point.

subtopics.title: RCU read-side lifetime model

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Show removal prevents new lookup while preexisting readers retain storage lifetime. Identify how refcount acquisition extends ownership beyond a read-side section and why the section alone does not do so.

Implement and investigate: Implement kl_grace with events0 enter reader bit id0..7,1 leave,2 retire,3 reclaim. Enter rejects duplicate IDs and admission after retirement; leave requires membership. Retirement is idempotent. Reclaim succeeds only after retirement with no readers and clears retired. This fixed-reader model is intentionally stronger than general RCU and must be mapped critically to the real primitive.

Falsify and transfer: Repair immediate reclamation on unlink; delayed arbitrary sleeps are not grace-period proofs. Host bitmask traces cannot validate actual RCU memory ordering. Then Permit readers of a replacement object after retirement; tag reader epochs and show waiting for all new readers can cause unnecessary starvation.

subtopics.title: Versioned kernel control records

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Demonstrate exact-length admission and byte-order independence; distinguish ABI versioning from ISO C object representation and kernel/user pointer validation.

Implement and investigate: Implement kl_decode on octets [version=1,length=2,lo,hi]. Require exactly4 bytes, decode little-endian16 into unsigned output, and leave it unchanged on all rejection. Then design a fixed-width ioctl or read/write adapter without embedding host pointers, documenting compatibility behavior.

Falsify and transfer: Repair acceptance of a mismatched embedded length and a cast of unaligned user bytes to a native struct. A correctly decoded version does not authorize an operation. Then Add a version2 optional field while preserving version1 bytes; compare strict rejection, ignorable extensions and per-operation authorization with adversarial tails.

subtopics.title: Unload defense and integrated lifetime audit

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Construct a global ownership graph and identify the linearization point of shutdown. Give separate evidence for module pinning, object release, callback quiescence and bounded wait policy.

Implement and investigate: Implement kl_can_unload(open_handles,pending_callbacks,closed) returning true only for closed==1 and both counts zero. Reject closed>1. Integrate the previous model with the teaching module: enumerate every close, completion and last-put ordering and provide a guest unload dossier showing why no callback can reach released state or unloaded text.

Falsify and transfer: A module unloads after the last open handle while a callback still retains its function pointer. Demonstrate rejection in the model; any guest fault stays inside the disposable VM. Then Add hot-unplug while two open handles remain: choose revoked operations versus retained detached objects, and justify error propagation and final cleanup under both close orders.

domains.title: RISC-V and AArch64 execution ports
domains.depth: derivation, implementation, falsification and delayed transfer

subtopics.title: Stack extent and ABI alignment

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Prove result<=top-bytes, alignment and nonwrap; account for consumed padding and live stack bounds.

Implement and investigate: Implement po_stack(top,bytes,out): require bytes<=top, subtract and round down to16-byte alignment; publish only on success. Treat integers as modeled addresses, not dereferenceable C pointers. Then build both assembly entry stubs with a private aligned stack and inspect the map.

Falsify and transfer: A port aligns to8 because pointers are8 bytes, violating the16-byte call boundary. A linker-defined top is not proof that subtraction stays in the reserved stack. Then Change to RV32E or Thumb and derive the appropriate ABI alignment from its specification rather than inheriting16. Add a guard region and test exact exhaustion.

subtopics.title: Callee state and platform registers

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Identify which owner saves each register and why the return-address register needs protection in nonleaf callees despite its caller-saved classification.

Implement and investigate: Implement po_saved(arch,reg), with arch0 RV64 integer ABI and arch1 AArch64. Report saved integer registers: RV x2,x8,x9,x18..x27; Arm x19..x29 and synthetic register31 for SP. Other fields return0. Independently compare hostile-caller assembly against the declared set; exclude x18 from portable allocation.

Falsify and transfer: A context port omits SP or assumes Arm x18 is a temporary everywhere. Explain a source-level test that can pass while this latent ABI violation remains. Then Add floating-point state and compare only low64 preservation of selected AArch64 SIMD registers against full vector context requirements.

subtopics.title: Argument register exhaustion

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive the first stack argument relative to entry SP; distinguish entry-SP offsets from offsets after the callee allocates its frame.

Implement and investigate: Implement po_arg(index,reg,offset) for the deliberately restricted nine-or-fewer uint64_t scalar interface: index0..7 maps to abstract argument registers0..7 with offset0; index8..15 maps to regUINT_MAX and stack offset8*(index-8); index>=16 rejects transactionally. The assembly adapter translates abstract registers to a0..a7 or x0..x7.

Falsify and transfer: A callee reads the ninth argument one slot above its defined location. All eight-register tests pass; the hostile ninth argument must falsify it. Then Return a large aggregate through a hidden result pointer and show why this scalar classifier cannot simply shift the same table on every ABI.

subtopics.title: Owned context images

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Prove a save/restore preserves exactly the declared set and leaves nonowned registers untouched. State stack ownership, resume-address validity and exclusion of asynchronous FP/trap state.

Implement and investigate: Implement po_save(dst,arch,registers) copying only po_saved registers into a zero-filled32-slot image; reject arch>1 before mutation. po_restore validates image arch equals requested arch and copies only saved slots into a live register model, preserving others. Destination/source are disjoint. Extend assembly context switches using the same documented offsets.

Falsify and transfer: Repair restoration of an RV image as Arm by rejecting mismatched tags before any register mutation. A C struct size match does not establish semantic compatibility. Then Add two task stacks and a yield-return continuation; inject stack exhaustion and duplicate resume, and compare cooperative with asynchronous preemption save sets.

subtopics.title: Signed immediates and relocation ranges

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive sign-extension using unsigned extraction and subtraction in a range representable by int. Separate field representability, target instruction alignment and linker relaxation.

Implement and investigate: Implement po_sign12(raw) for the low12 bits as a mathematical signed value -2048..2047, ignoring higher bits. Implement po_branch(delta,bits,align) accepting only bits2..30, align2 or4 and aligned signed delta in [-2^(bits-1),2^(bits-1)-align]. Use this as a relocation admission oracle, not as a complete instruction encoder.

Falsify and transfer: Truncating an odd branch displacement silently redirects execution. A range-only check is insufficient; a passing assembler can still hide linker-added veneers. Then Encode RV B/J immediate bit scattering and compare with an independent assembler, then force an out-of-range AArch64 call and inspect its veneer clobbers.

subtopics.title: Trap status versus call state

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Draw status before entry, after entry and after return. Explain which processor state is automatic, which is software saved and why a call-return instruction cannot replace a trap return.

Implement and investigate: Implement po_trap(status,from_supervisor) and po_return(status): trap records spp, copies sie to spie and clears sie; return restores sie from spie, sets spie1 and clears spp. Inputs are boolean fields; invalid input rejects without mutation. Compare the explicit model to supervisor CSR traces in a dedicated RV guest.

Falsify and transfer: Repair stale prior-privilege state after return and a nested handler that overwrites the first saved PC. The model cannot establish interrupt controller acknowledgement behavior. Then Port the same logical event to an AArch64 exception level and identify every register/return difference from an inspected architecture manual before implementing.

subtopics.title: Privilege-aware memory access

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive each access decision before dereferencing and identify omitted page-walk obligations: validity, canonical address, superpage alignment, access/dirty updates, translation synchronization and fault cause.

Implement and investigate: Implement po_access(user_page,supervisor,sum,mxr,r,w,x,operation), with boolean flags and op0 read,1 write,2 execute. User execution rejects supervisor-only pages. Supervisor execution always rejects user pages; supervisor reads/writes user pages require sum. Read requires r or mxr&&x; write requires w; execute requires x. This models the inspected SUM/MXR obligations, not a complete page walk.

Falsify and transfer: Repair a supervisor execute path that assumes SUM permits executing user memory. A model allow decision never grants C pointer provenance or physical access. Then Implement a bounded three-level page-table walker with synthetic tables, then compare RV64 Sv39 and the selected Arm translation regime; inspect their full manuals and record unresolved differences.

subtopics.title: Link closure and changed-target defense

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Distinguish declarations, emitted references, linked providers and actually exercised target paths. Explain why hosted test libraries cannot be treated as target dependencies.

Implement and investigate: Implement po_closure(required_mask,provided_mask) returning true exactly when every required helper bit has an approved implementation. Bits represent memcpy, division, atomic fallback and stack protector for the synthetic map. Then derive the real closure from nm/readelf/map output for both ports and record every unresolved or policy-disallowed symbol.

Falsify and transfer: A port links only because the developer machine supplies libgcc or libc; removing the runtime reveals a hidden helper. Report this as missing target support, not a compiler bug. Then Change optimization, atomics width and ISA extensions; regenerate closure and code-size/stack evidence and explain every new helper or inline expansion.

domains.title: Firmware lifecycle and recoverable updates
domains.depth: derivation, implementation, falsification and delayed transfer

subtopics.title: Flash programming as a constrained state change

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Prove admission catches every forbidden bit transition and prevents a partially modified prefix. Derive physical program-unit alignment and erase-sector dependencies separately.

Implement and investigate: Implement lc_program(dst,src,n) on live disjoint octet spans: reject if any new byte requests a0-to-1 transition, leaving all bytes unchanged; otherwise program with bitwise AND. n0 succeeds. This is an atomic admission model, not a claim that physical multi-byte programming is atomic.

Falsify and transfer: Repair a model that silently ANDs an illegal request and reports success. Its resulting bytes differ from the requested image even without a crash. Then Replace whole-span admission by per-program-unit persistence and cut power after each unit; derive which metadata must stay uncommitted until image completion.

subtopics.title: Integrity without authenticity

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive one byte update by polynomial division and state the initialization/reflection/finalization conventions. Explain collision possibility and absence of a secret authentication key.

Implement and investigate: Implement lc_crc using reflected CRC-32 polynomial0xedb88320, initial state0xffffffff and final complement, processing bytes low-bit first. No CRC library. Verify empty input and123456789, then construct an altered payload with a recomputed checksum and explain why it still lacks authorization.

Falsify and transfer: A verifier omits the final complement and rejects valid images; another accepts attacker-recomputed CRC as a signature. Only the first defect is covered by numeric test anchors. Then Add a separately verified signature API that returns an explicit verdict and key identifier; inject fail-open and stale-key responses without implementing production cryptography in this exercise.

subtopics.title: Authenticated image admission

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Specify exactly which bytes and metadata the trusted verifier authenticates; derive bounded extent arithmetic and the immutable authority for the rollback floor.

Implement and investigate: Implement lc_admit(length,slot_capacity,version,floor,signature_ok): accept only length1..capacity, version>=floor and signature_ok exactly1. The verifier verdict is injected by the harness; it is not derived from a learner-controlled flag in a real image. Return0 for all invalid requests before any slot selection.

Falsify and transfer: The intentionally faulty admission ignores a failed verifier verdict. Harmless success is selection of a synthetic unauthorized image; no real key or deployed bootloader is targeted. Then Introduce key rotation and a revoked signing key; show why a numerically newer version with a valid old-key signature may still be inadmissible.

subtopics.title: Trial boot, confirmation and rollback

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Prove repeated unconfirmed resets eventually return to a known confirmed slot. Identify the exact persistence point before transferring control and the risk if it occurs afterward.

Implement and investigate: Implement lc_select on LCBoot with active and trial slots0/1, confirmed and attempted booleans. If confirmed select active. If unconfirmed and not attempted, select trial and persist attempted1. On later unconfirmed reset select active. Reject invalid fields before output. The model treats attempted persistence as one atomic record; later projects remove that assumption.

Falsify and transfer: The faulty state machine retries the unconfirmed image forever, causing a boot loop. A watchdog reset alone cannot repair an incorrect persistent selection policy. Then Require two-core health confirmation on H745 and inject one core failing after the other confirms; define a joint image-generation commit and recovery protocol.

subtopics.title: Redundant journal and torn commit records

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Enumerate crashes after each field write and before/after marker programming. State why the XOR check is a synthetic torn-write control, not an authentication mechanism or robust error code.

Implement and investigate: Implement lc_journal_select over two LCJournal records. A valid record has commit0xa5 and check==seq XOR value XOR0x5a5a5a5a. Select the valid record with greatest nonwrapping seq; equal valid seq with unequal values is ambiguous and rejects. Return selected index through output only on success. Sequence exhaustion requires a migration policy, not wraparound.

Falsify and transfer: Repair selection of an uncommitted newer record and ambiguous equal-generation records. Numerical sequence comparison is invalid after uncontrolled wrap. Then Replace the atomic marker with a multi-byte program unit that can tear; derive a coding/validation rule and prove at least one old or new valid record survives each allowed fault.

subtopics.title: Monotonic security floor

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive the invariant floor never decreases and analyze the confirmation/floor ordering under reset. State the threat model for storage tampering and what a RAM model cannot enforce.

Implement and investigate: Implement lc_raise_floor(current,candidate,confirmed,out): require confirmed exactly1 and candidate>=current; publish candidate on success. Reject rollback or unconfirmed advancement transactionally. Compose it with boot confirmation and identify the trusted persistence needed in real firmware.

Falsify and transfer: The faulty update accepts a smaller floor from an otherwise valid image. A signed image is not permission to weaken anti-rollback policy. Then Introduce a finite monotonic counter that reaches exhaustion; design a fail-closed recovery/key-rotation protocol without silently wrapping its security epoch.

subtopics.title: Dual-core update quiescence

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Prove no old-generation peer can retain writable storage at update commit. Separate cache visibility, notification delivery and logical acknowledgement.

Implement and investigate: Implement lc_peer_ready(local_epoch,ack_epoch,outstanding) accepting only equal epochs and zero outstanding transfers. Use it in a two-core shutdown model: close admission, drain DMA/IPC owners, obtain an epoch-specific acknowledgement, then permit update. A stale acknowledgement must never unlock a new generation.

Falsify and transfer: Repair acceptance of a stale acknowledgement after independent peer reboot. A memory barrier cannot repair the missing generation check. Then Move shared metadata from noncacheable SRAM to cacheable SRAM; derive cache-line ownership/maintenance and repeat physical traces on the dedicated H745 board.

subtopics.title: Fault capture and recovery evidence

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Define record validity, persistence assumptions, reset-reason interpretation and ownership of storage during recovery; corrupted PC values must never become executable addresses.

Implement and investigate: Implement lc_capture_valid(words,n) for exactly4 uint32_t words [reason,pc,check,commit], check=reason XOR pc XOR0x9e3779b9 and commit0xc0de. Reject wrong count, invalid check or missing marker. Build a minimal firmware crash record producer that writes commit last and never allocates, then cut the model after every store.

Falsify and transfer: Repair a record reader that accepts a committed but corrupted payload. A synthetic check detects only its modeled faults; physical retention and fault-entry register capture remain separate. Then Add nested faults and a full crash log; choose preserve-first versus preserve-latest policy, prove bounded writes and assess what diagnostic information is lost.

domains.title: A C-subset compiler with original x86-64 and Thumb backends
domains.depth: derivation, implementation, falsification and delayed transfer

subtopics.title: Bounded lexer with exact progress

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive the pre-multiply bound and exact consumed extent, including an unterminated span. Explain why end-of-input is a successful token distinct from rejection.

Implement and investigate: Implement cc_token over a nonterminated byte span. Skip ASCII space/newline/tab; recognize decimal0..65535(kind1), x(2), ((3), )(4), +(5), *(6), and end(0). Return1 on token/end,0 on invalid or overflow. On failure preserve offset/kind/value. On success set value0 except constants. Do not call strtol or a lexer library.

Falsify and transfer: Repair overflow accepted through unchecked decimal accumulation and a scanner that consumes a bad byte before reporting its location. Then Add hexadecimal constants and comments; distinguish preprocessing tokens from semantic tokens and preserve exact diagnostic spans without accepting partial malformed literals.

subtopics.title: Precedence parser and bounded syntax construction

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Prove each parser level consumes its grammar production or rejects, and derive linear token work with bounded recursion. Explain why no partially constructed IR is publishable.

Implement and investigate: Implement cc_parse from the declared expression grammar, generating postfix CONST/ARG/ADD/MUL followed by RET. Multiplication binds tighter than addition; parentheses override. Limit nesting to16 and IR capacity to caller storage. On failure used remains unchanged; partially written IR scratch is unspecified and must never be executed. Reject every unconsumed nonspace byte.

Falsify and transfer: A parser accepts the valid prefix2 of2? and silently drops the error. Another implements2+3*x as(2+3)*x. Separate tokenization, grouping and lowering defects. Then Add subtraction and left associativity, then introduce a side-effecting call and state which source sequencing must be preserved rather than inferred from precedence.

subtopics.title: Subset type and arithmetic semantics

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive modulo behavior independently of host signed overflow; identify absent signed conversions, floating-point rules and pointer semantics rather than pretending they are covered.

Implement and investigate: Implement cc_binary(op,a,b,out) for op3 addition and4 multiplication modulo2^32, using uint64_t intermediates and explicit conversion. Reject other opcodes without changing output. Identify the host assumptions required by uint32_t/uint64_t and compare with the C unsigned-return wrapper.

Falsify and transfer: A backend replaces multiplication by addition or performs signed overflow in its evaluator. Passing small positive constants is insufficient evidence. Then Add a signed32 type with explicit overflow diagnostics, usual arithmetic conversions and casts; construct a case where the unsigned and signed programs must differ.

subtopics.title: Typed intermediate representation and interpreter

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Associate every opcode with input/output type and stack effect; prove validated execution cannot underflow/overflow its bounded stack and returns the expression denotation.

Implement and investigate: Implement cc_run over verified CCIns with a local64-entry uint32_t stack and one x argument. CONST and ARG push; ADD/MUL consume two and push one; RET must be last with exactly one value. Reject malformed streams and preserve output. Use cc_binary for semantic arithmetic, not native signed expressions.

Falsify and transfer: A nominal interpreter reports success without publishing the computed result, while another executes malformed IR before checking its stack effects. Then Add basic blocks and conditional branches; derive join-state type/stack compatibility and bound or explicitly budget loops before extending execution.

subtopics.title: Intermediate representation verification and resource bounds

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive prefix-height and terminal-height conditions and peak stack bytes separately for the two backends. Explain the verifier assumptions that remain outside its scope.

Implement and investigate: Implement cc_validate for1..128 instructions, at most64 live stack values, constants<=65535, opcodes1..5, no underflow, and exactly one final RET with height1. Return peak depth only on success. Reject any operation after RET and any missing RET.

Falsify and transfer: The faulty verifier accepts executable instructions after RET. That can conceal malformed data and causes consumers to disagree about the authoritative program extent. Then Serialize IR to a bytecode file; add version, checked count arithmetic and canonical endianness, then fuzz parser and verifier independently.

subtopics.title: Original x86-64 code emission

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Map each IR stack transition to emitted instructions, prove balanced machine stack and identify all clobbered registers. The textual anchor is weaker than assembling and executing the result.

Implement and investigate: Implement cc_x86 emitting NUL-terminated GNU assembly for cm_expr(unsigned x) from valid IR using edi input, eax result, rcx temporary and64-bit push/pop storage. Use bounded staging so too-small output capacity leaves caller bytes unchanged. No LLVM, compiler library or template compiler may replace emission.

Falsify and transfer: The mutant lowers multiply as addition. A different faulty emitter uses64-bit multiply without the required unsigned32 truncation. Differential execution must expose the semantic mismatch. Then Add an actual function call: preserve argument x across it, restore16-byte call alignment and compare caller-saved/callee-saved decisions under nested expressions.

subtopics.title: Original Thumb code emission

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Prove the private operand stack remains word-aligned and returns to its public8-byte boundary. Identify the Thumb-state return and why r3 would not survive a newly added call.

Implement and investigate: Implement cc_thumb emitting Thumb-2 GNU assembly using r3 to retain x, r0/r1 temporaries, word pushes/pops and bx lr. Constants fit movw. No nested calls or FP operations are supported. Stage output transactionally and preserve the exact same unsigned32 semantics as x86.

Falsify and transfer: The backend omits argument preservation, so expressions that load x after a constant compute from the constant instead. A constant-only test cannot detect this. Then Retarget Thumb-1 without movw or the same instruction set assumptions; synthesize constants, inspect helper dependencies and execute on the corresponding emulator CPU.

subtopics.title: Differential compiler validation and translation limits

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Separate front-end correctness, IR semantics, backend correctness and target environment. Define the supported source subset before interpreting an oracle disagreement.

Implement and investigate: Implement cc_compile_eval(source,n,x,out) composing parser, verifier and interpreter with bounded128-instruction storage. Preserve output on any failure. Generate valid expression trees independently, render source and mathematical denotation, then compare interpreter and both emitted targets. Minimize a mismatch while retaining its semantic predicate.

Falsify and transfer: An integrated path perturbs an otherwise correct result; a shared parser-based expected value would reproduce some parser faults and miss them. Use independently generated trees. Then Add variables, conditionals, loops and function calls in separate increments with revised grammar, IR verifier and both backends; retain counterexamples at each boundary and state any still-unimplemented C construct.

domains.title: Formal verification, falsification and fuzzing
domains.depth: derivation, implementation, falsification and delayed transfer

subtopics.title: Bitvector arithmetic and complete bounds

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive the pre-add inequality without executing overflowing signed arithmetic. Prove unchanged output on failure as a separate postcondition and identify pointer validity assumptions.

Implement and investigate: Implement vf_add(a,b,out) for uint32_t: return1 and sum when representable, else0 with unchanged output. Write a CBMC harness for every input and a sentinel output, with overflow checks enabled; separately exhaust a reduced8-bit domain and explain why that enumeration is not a proof for32-bit implementation code.

Falsify and transfer: Repair wrapping arithmetic that reports success and a harness that assumes away every overflow input. Demonstrate a witness satisfying the assumptions and violating the mutant. Then Generalize to checked multiplication and mixed-width conversion, deriving a new precondition rather than mechanically substituting the addition predicate.

subtopics.title: Loop invariants and binary-search termination

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Prove all indices below lo are<key, all at/above hi are>=key, and hi-lo strictly decreases. Derive memory bounds and handle duplicate values without changing the intended first-position contract.

Implement and investigate: Implement vf_lower_bound on a sorted nondecreasing uint32_t array, returning the first index with value>=key or n. Use half-open[lo,hi), calculate midpoint without overflow and retain O(log n) comparisons. Empty input permits a null array. Establish sortedness as a precondition, not a fact proved by a search test.

Falsify and transfer: A <= comparison implements upper_bound, which passes unique-key examples. An incorrect midpoint update can also loop forever on a singleton interval. Then Change to a descending comparator and an opaque record key; rederive the invariant and verify comparator consistency assumptions instead of copying inequalities.

subtopics.title: Stateful property harness and ownership

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Prove size conservation and rejection atomicity at each step; define ownership of queued elements separately from the scalar ring indices. Explain why an oracle sharing the same count representation could reproduce the defect.

Implement and investigate: Implement vf_ring_step for VFRing with positive capacity, head<capacity, size<=capacity. op0 push rejects full and increments size; op1 pop rejects empty, advances head modulo capacity and decrements size. Reject invalid state or operation without mutation. Build a sequence harness using a Python list oracle and generation from valid/invalid transition classes.

Falsify and transfer: The mutant permits a push into a full ring, producing size>capacity. A final pop-only test can conceal this intermediate violation. Then Add borrowed payloads with destructor callbacks and injected construction failure; extend the model to exactly-once lifetime obligations and reentrant callback restrictions.

subtopics.title: Parser fuzzing with semantic oracles

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Separate memory-safety, grammar, integrity and canonicalization properties; bound fuzz input processing without excluding empty, malformed or huge harness inputs.

Implement and investigate: Implement vf_frame for bytes[length,payload...,xor]. Require n>=2, length<=16, exact n=length+2 and XOR of payload equal final byte; publish length only on success. Empty payload is valid with bytes[0,0]. Fuzz all inputs0..64 bytes, check round-trip canonical encoding on success and output sentinel on failure.

Falsify and transfer: The parser ignores checksum mismatch yet never crashes, so sanitizer-only fuzzing misses the defect. The semantic oracle must reject the corrupted frame. Then Introduce streaming segmentation and state reset between repeated calls; compare every split with the single-shot decoder and minimize a split-sensitive mismatch.

subtopics.title: Counterexample minimization

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Prove predicate preservation after each deletion and justify termination. Distinguish1-minimality from globally optimal shrinking and discuss order-dependent outcomes.

Implement and investigate: Implement vf_shrink for an in-place byte vector of length at most65535 whose failure predicate is sum(bytes)>=threshold. Greedily remove each byte when the remaining sum still fails; retry the same position after removal. Return final length. If the original does not fail, leave it unchanged. The result is1-minimal under deletion, not globally shortest.

Falsify and transfer: The faulty shrinker increments its index after deletion, skipping the shifted byte and leaving a removable element. A merely smaller result is not the stated minimality guarantee. Then Shrink an event schedule while preserving the same violated lifecycle invariant and first divergent transition, rather than preserving any nonzero exit.

subtopics.title: Bounded schedule exploration

objectives.text: Derive and defend: State the safety invariant released implies completed and derive every reachable state. Explain which liveness claims require a scheduler/environment assumption beyond finite enumeration.

Implement and investigate: Implement vf_request for events0 submit,1 cancel,2 complete,3 release. Submit once; cancellation only after submit and before completion; complete once after submit whether or not cancelled; release only after completion and only once. Enumerate all event words through length6 and compare state/rejection to an independent transition relation.

Falsify and transfer: The mutant releases on cancellation before completion, allowing a late callback to access released storage. A mutex alone does not fix the incorrect state transition. Then Split submission and publication into separate steps, add two actors and a weak-memory litmus; identify which additional ordering assumptions need model checking or target evidence.

subtopics.title: Deterministic fuzz harness composition

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive the required isolation between fuzz invocations, including allocator cleanup and thread joining. Distinguish deterministic input-derived randomness from wall-clock seeding.

Implement and investigate: Implement vf_digest(frame,n,out): validate with vf_frame, then derive a32-bit rolling digest starting from0 for that input only, digest=digest*33+byte across payload bytes. Preserve output on invalid input. Repeated A,B,A calls must give the same results for A. Keep corpus generation and sanitizer runtime outside the target dependency graph.

Falsify and transfer: The mutant retains the prior hash globally, creating a history-dependent mismatch. A single fresh-process run passes and therefore misses the defect. Then Deliberately fuzz a multi-command protocol where history is meaningful; encode the entire session in one input and reset only between sessions.

subtopics.title: Proof claim audit and independent transfer

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Bind the claim to source, compiler/solver configuration, assumptions, model bound and checked properties. Explain why local self-reported flags cannot establish reviewer independence or tool honesty.

Implement and investigate: Implement vf_claim(tool_success,unwinding_complete,assumptions_witnessed,unchecked_properties): accept a bounded-proof receipt only when the first three flags are exactly1 and unchecked count0. Use this predicate as a checklist, not a cryptographic verifier, and audit the saved CBMC/fuzz campaigns against actual logs and source hashes.

Falsify and transfer: A receipt omits complete unwinding but labels a loop universally safe. Reproduce the missing iteration counterexample and narrow the claim before attempting a genuine inductive proof. Then Audit a new allocator or parser without the worked harness; choose proof, fuzzing and differential methods based on mechanisms and defend residual gaps after seven days.

domains.title: Advanced Linux I/O and completion ownership
domains.depth: derivation, implementation, falsification and delayed transfer

subtopics.title: Vectored partial progress

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Prove accepted progress plus remaining extent equals the original stream length, including zero spans and overflow. Distinguish kernel acceptance from remote delivery or persistence.

Implement and investigate: Implement li_advance(lengths,count,position,bytes) for a valid vector cursor. Compute remaining extent with checked size_t arithmetic, reject excess progress transactionally, then advance across zero-length elements and normalize the terminal position to{count,0}. This is caller-side accounting, not a writev replacement.

Falsify and transfer: The faulty cursor resets the within-element offset after a short write, duplicating the first byte of the next span on retry. Then Add EINTR, EAGAIN and an error after a nonzero prefix; define whether the API returns progress plus deferred error or an immediate terminal error and test consumers.

subtopics.title: Edge readiness and fair draining

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Distinguish kernel notification, locally remembered readiness and actual EAGAIN. Derive a fairness budget that does not lose readiness or spin forever after EOF.

Implement and investigate: Implement li_ready_after(result,budget_exhausted) for a synthetic read result: positive progress retains readiness, -2 means EAGAIN and clears readiness,0 EOF clears readiness,-1 terminal error clears readiness. Return1 while progress remains, even when a dispatch budget was exhausted. Exercise the actual anonymous-pipe EPOLLET adapter and compare drain-to-EAGAIN with a local ready queue.

Falsify and transfer: The mutant clears readiness at budget exhaustion while unread data remains. The pipe receives no new edge, exposing a liveness failure without a crash. Then Add two continuously active peers and timerfd deadlines; prove bounded dispatch work and measure fairness under equivalent correctness contracts.

subtopics.title: Shared submission ring arithmetic

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive the bounded-distance interpretation under counter wrap. Separate single-producer ownership, ring-slot lifetime and payload-before-tail publication.

Implement and investigate: Implement li_slot(head,tail,capacity,out) for uint32_t monotonic counters: capacity is a power of two in1..2^30, unsigned tail-head must be<capacity, and output is tail&(capacity-1). Reject invalid/full states unchanged. Then map the arithmetic to raw io_uring offsets and acquire/release operations after feature probing.

Falsify and transfer: A producer masks tail and overwrites a still-owned full slot. Adding a barrier cannot repair missing capacity admission. Then Add multiple producers or change queue depth away from a power of two; redesign reservation and indexing rather than reusing the single-owner mask proof.

subtopics.title: Generation-tagged completion ownership

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Prove each target completion is consumed once and cannot authorize release of another generation. State finite-generation exhaustion policy and metadata versus payload lifetime.

Implement and investigate: Implement li_event on LIRequest with state0 idle,1 submitted,2 cancel-requested,3 completed,4 released. Events0 submit,1 request cancel,2 target completion(result),3 release. Require matching generation for every event. Completion is allowed from1/2 once; release only from3 once. Failed transitions preserve the object.

Falsify and transfer: The mutant ignores generation and lets a stale completion finish a new request. Demonstrate harmless wrong-result publication using two synthetic requests, not another process’s data. Then Add multishot operations where nonterminal completions retain ownership; derive terminal recognition and buffer recycling from the actual opcode flags.

subtopics.title: Cancellation acknowledgement versus target completion

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Name separate ownership of cancel request, target request and payload. Explain how success, not-found and already-completing cancellation results change scheduling but do not substitute for a target terminal event.

Implement and investigate: Implement li_releasable(cancel_ack,target_terminal) accepting only boolean inputs and returning target_terminal. Build a two-CQE schedule harness that permutes cancellation completion, target completion and close; inspect actual io_uring cancellation result codes on the original temporary-file/pipe operations.

Falsify and transfer: The faulty adapter frees the target buffer when its cancel request completes, then processes a late target CQE. A sanitizer finding identifies a lifetime violation, not kernel exploitability. Then Add a timeout linked to a multishot request; enumerate which CQEs are terminal and determine whether the backend supports the requested cancellation semantics.

subtopics.title: Deadlines, timer events and wraparound

objectives.text: Derive and defend: State the half-range observation assumption and prove equality is expiration. Distinguish wall-clock corrections, monotonic elapsed time and deadline policy.

Implement and investigate: Implement li_expired(start,now,duration,out) for a wrapping32-bit tick model with duration1..2^31-1 and elapsed distance known below2^31. Set out when unsigned now-start>=duration. Reject invalid duration without changing out. Use timerfd in the Linux adapter and keep real monotonic timestamps separate from modeled ticks.

Falsify and transfer: The faulty start+duration comparison wraps the deadline and expires an operation prematurely. Resetting the total deadline after each byte also permits indefinite slow progress. Then Combine idle and total deadlines with eventfd shutdown and signalfd notifications; measure cancellation latency without claiming observed maxima are universal bounds.

subtopics.title: Durable replacement and power-loss cuts

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Specify observable atomicity, persistence, filesystem assumptions and failure recovery. Account for open descriptors to the replaced old inode and permissions on the new object.

Implement and investigate: Implement li_durable(write_done,file_synced,renamed,directory_synced) requiring all flags exactly1. Then write a local temporary-file replacement adapter: write fully, fsync the new file, rename within its temporary directory, fsync that directory, and report exactly which stage failed. Use a synthetic crash-cut ledger; do not claim real power-loss durability from a normal process exit.

Falsify and transfer: A program reports durable success after rename but before directory synchronization. Its normal readback passes while a crash can invalidate the stated guarantee. Then Change filesystem, mount options and cross-directory replacement; derive which ordering/atomicity arguments and crash experiments must be repeated.

subtopics.title: Zero-copy claims and retained buffers

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Distinguish copy avoidance, kernel retention, DMA mapping and application borrowing. Derive memory-pressure/backpressure costs and what the selected syscall actually promises.

Implement and investigate: Implement li_buffer_release(submitted,terminal,borrowers) returning true only when submitted/terminal are booleans, every submitted operation is terminal, and borrowers0. Use it to compare read/write, sendfile/splice and a mapped-buffer path over synthetic local files; measure bytes copied, syscalls, CPU time and retained memory under the same output contract.

Falsify and transfer: The mutant releases after terminal I/O while an application borrower still uses the buffer. Kernel completion does not revoke independent application ownership. Then Introduce direct I/O alignment constraints and unsupported-filesystem errors; preserve a semantically equivalent fallback and measure overhead without silently changing durability.

domains.title: Memory safety offense and defense in original teaching programs
domains.depth: derivation, implementation, falsification and delayed transfer

subtopics.title: Spatial bounds and a harmless overwrite witness

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive subtraction-form bounds without overflow and distinguish logical isolation from ISO C allocated-object bounds. State why a sentinel violation proves integrity failure only within the teaching model.

Implement and investigate: Implement md_write(arena,logical_capacity,offset,input,n) for an original32-byte arena. Reject capacity>31, offset>capacity or n>capacity-offset before any write; write only the admitted span. Byte31 is a sentinel outside the logical object. Compare with the supplied faulty teaching path that validates only the32-byte physical extent; attacker controls offset/n/data and harmless success is sentinel change.

Falsify and transfer: Repair capacity confusion and post-write checks. A canary that detects corruption afterward does not restore overwritten data or authorize the write. Then Split the logical object into a real heap allocation and run the isolated faulty path under ASan; compare deterministic model evidence with environment-dependent undefined execution and mitigation effects.

subtopics.title: Allocation arithmetic and truncation

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive the allocation and subsequent access extents in the same value domain. Identify every narrowing conversion and the branch that incorrectly authorizes it.

Implement and investigate: Implement md_extent(count,stride,limit,out) using uint32_t inputs and uint64_t arithmetic; accept only product<=limit and product<=UINT32_MAX, publish the product on success, otherwise preserve out. Compare against a teaching allocator that truncates product to16 bits before checking. Do not actually allocate attacker-sized memory.

Falsify and transfer: The original local mutant requests8193 elements of8 bytes, validates a truncated8-byte allocation and would later copy65544 bytes. Demonstrate the admitted size mismatch without performing the dangerous copy. Then Change data model and add alignment/header overhead; rederive all multiplication/addition/conversion bounds and explain whether the same attacker input still reaches the defect.

subtopics.title: Temporal identity and stale access

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Prove a stale token cannot authorize current-incarnation access, state the trusted token origin and require retirement before generation wrap. Compare with an actual heap use-after-free sanitizer target without treating allocator reuse as guaranteed.

Implement and investigate: Implement md_read(arena,claimed_generation,index,out): require live==1, matching generation and index<16 before publishing a byte. Failed reads leave out unchanged. The original arena remains allocated, so the stale-handle witness is defined C behavior; attacker retains an old token across reuse and attempts to read a new synthetic occupant.

Falsify and transfer: The mutant ignores generation and reveals a new occupant’s synthetic byte through an old token. This demonstrates a confidentiality violation in the target, not a read primitive against another process. Then Add asynchronous completion retaining a token, then release/reuse the slot before completion. Design cancellation and retirement so old callbacks cannot expose the new occupant.

subtopics.title: Owned arena views and authorization

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Specify representation, operations, ownership and failure semantics of a checked view. Identify exactly what runtime checks enforce and what trusted-caller discipline or external verification must guarantee.

Implement and investigate: Implement md_authorize(arena,principal,generation,begin,length): require live1, exact owner and generation, begin<=16 and length<=16-begin; return admission only, without exposing a pointer on failure. principal is supplied by a trusted harness channel, not copied from request bytes. Define the trusted boundary and compare with a forged-request owner field.

Falsify and transfer: The mutant validates generation and bounds but ignores principal ownership. The attacker can read another synthetic principal’s object without any memory error or sanitizer report. Then Compare the C view with a language-enforced borrow or capability mechanism; provide a concrete C counterexample showing forged structs or escaped pointers defeat an overstated equivalence claim.

subtopics.title: Bounded control-flow corruption analysis

objectives.text: Derive and defend: State attacker control, target-local effect and limits. Distinguish data-only unauthorized dispatch from demonstrated arbitrary code execution; analyze control-flow integrity separately from operation authorization.

Implement and investigate: Implement md_dispatch(op,grant,sentinel) with op0 read-only no-op and op1 set sentinel77, allowed only when trusted grant==1. Reject unknown op and nonboolean grant before mutation. Analyze the supplied intentionally flawed dispatcher that checks only op range; attacker-controlled op1 without grant must change only the synthetic sentinel in the faulty build.

Falsify and transfer: A valid indirect-call target can still perform an unauthorized operation. Bounds checks and a control-flow whitelist do not replace the grant check. Then Add a table of three trusted callbacks and a corrupted index inside the original program; compare range checks, read-only dispatch tables and compiler CFI while recording only observed target effects.

subtopics.title: Format-string authority and byte-preserving logging

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Identify which argument is interpreted as a format and prove the repaired path treats attacker bytes as data. Discuss embedded NUL, truncation policy and logging integrity separately.

Implement and investigate: Implement md_log_copy(input,n,output,capacity) copying exact bytes and appending NUL, requiring n<capacity and no overlap; failure leaves output unchanged. Percent bytes have no interpretation. Compare an original isolated printf(user_format) target using the fixed synthetic string%n and a supplied local integer pointer with printf("%s",user_text); the harmless witness is only that integer changing.

Falsify and transfer: Blindly replacing percent with a question mark suppresses the witness but corrupts the required logged bytes. The real repair separates interpreter control from untrusted data. Then Add structured binary logging with explicit length and escaping at display time; test embedded NUL and terminal-control bytes without confusing storage fidelity with safe rendering.

subtopics.title: Exactly-once release and error cleanup

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Prove ownership conservation and exactly-one destructor call under every failure prefix. Explain why nulling one alias cannot revoke another copied raw pointer.

Implement and investigate: Implement md_release(MDOwner) requiring owned exactly1, setting owned0 and incrementing releases once. Repeat release returns0 unchanged. Reject a release counter atUINT_MAX before state change. Build an allocation/failure schedule with caller, queue and callback owners and record every transfer.

Falsify and transfer: The faulty cleanup path releases twice after ownership moved to a callback. Demonstrate the duplicate counter first, then separately observe an actual original double-free target under ASan. Then Introduce reentrant destruction and partial object construction; define callback restrictions or use detached cleanup state so recursive calls cannot double release.

subtopics.title: Observable work, timing and mitigation limits

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Separate functional equality, source-level work count, emitted branches and measured timing. State memory-validity, compiler and CPU assumptions and residual cache/power/speculation channels.

Implement and investigate: Implement md_equal(a,b,n,steps) scanning all n bytes, accumulating XOR difference, reporting steps=n and returning equality. Empty spans compare equal without dereference. Compare with an intentionally early-exit mutant using synthetic secrets only. Inspect optimized code and measure distributions without treating equal loop counts as a universal constant-time guarantee.

Falsify and transfer: The early-exit mutant reports only one step for a first-byte mismatch, leaking a prefix relation. ASan can remain clean because the defect is confidentiality, not invalid memory access. Then Change optimization, vectorization and unequal-length policy; derive what remains observable and compare hardened library behavior only as an external benchmark, not a replacement for the first-principles implementation.

domains.title: Numerical contracts and SIMD from first principles
domains.depth: derivation, implementation, falsification and delayed transfer

subtopics.title: Fixed-point scale, rounding and saturation

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive the product scale and prove int32_t multiplication and negation bounds before implementing absolute value. Separate saturation policy from the rounding rule.

Implement and investigate: Implement ns_q15(a,b) for signed Q1.15 operands: multiply exactly in int32_t, round the scaled result to nearest with ties away from zero, then saturate into [-32768,32767]. In particular -32768 times -32768 saturates to32767. Derive the range of every intermediate and distinguish quantization error from saturation.

Falsify and transfer: The mutant truncates toward zero, failing positive and negative half-way cases. A signed right shift is not a portable replacement for the specified rounding rule. Then Change to Q3.12 and compare wrap, saturate and error-return APIs. Derive a dot-product accumulator width from maximum length instead of copying the Q1.15 constants.

subtopics.title: Exact rounding model and ties to even

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive nearest-neighbor intervals and parity at exact ties. Prove remainder doubling is avoided by comparing r with denominator-r, and explain the negative sign symmetry.

Implement and investigate: Implement ns_round_even(numerator,denominator,out) for numerator in[-1000000,1000000] and denominator in[1,1000000]. Return the nearest integer, breaking exact ties toward an even integer; leave out unchanged on invalid input. Use integer quotient/remainder, with no floating conversion or rounding library.

Falsify and transfer: The mutant rounds every tie away from zero. A test corpus containing only odd lower endpoints misses the defect; a changed rounding mode cannot be assumed to affect every compiler-folded expression. Then Compare the rational oracle with volatile double operations under each available fenv rounding mode, retaining compiler flags and FENV_ACCESS support limits. Distinguish conversion behavior from arithmetic rounding.

subtopics.title: Exact accumulation bounds

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive the maximum positive and negative product and n-times-product bound. Explain which intermediate width is required before multiplication and before addition.

Implement and investigate: Implement ns_dot(a,b,n,out) for int16_t arrays and0<=n<=65535. Accumulate in int64_t and publish the exact sum; n==0 returns0 without reading either array. Reject n>65535 without changing out. No vector or BLAS library is permitted.

Falsify and transfer: The mutant narrows the completed sum to32 bits. On a target with a different conversion behavior, report implementation-defined narrowing separately from the violated mathematical output contract. Then Vectorize into several wide partial sums and compare exact results for every tail length. Change n beyond the proved bound and design checked partial accumulation without silently weakening exactness.

subtopics.title: Compensated reduction and cancellation

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive the correction for each magnitude ordering and identify every rounding point. Compare naive, compensated and exact-rational reference results without claiming a universal relative-error bound near a zero sum.

Implement and investigate: Implement ns_sum(a,n,out) using Neumaier compensated summation in the supplied order. Accept n<=65535 and finite inputs; reject any nonfinite intermediate or final result without modifying out. Empty input returns0. Assume binary64 and ordinary non-reassociated operations, and record these assumptions explicitly.

Falsify and transfer: The mutant drops compensation and returns0 for [1e16,1,-1e16]. Reassociation permitted by fast-math can invalidate the correction identity even when the source text is unchanged. Then Implement pairwise summation and a fixed reduction tree for parallel execution. Compare accuracy, stack use, reproducibility and throughput under an equivalent exceptional-value contract.

subtopics.title: Scaled norm and intermediate overflow

objectives.text: Derive and defend: State the scale/sumsq invariant in real arithmetic and discuss floating error separately. Prove why the ratio is bounded and identify final overflow as distinct from avoidable intermediate overflow.

Implement and investigate: Implement ns_norm(a,n,out) for at most65535 finite doubles using scaled sum of squares: retain scale and sumsq so intermediate squares are of ratios<=1. Empty/all-zero vectors return0. Reject nonfinite input or unrepresentable final norm without publishing output. fabs and sqrt are permitted primitives.

Falsify and transfer: The naive mutant squares3e200 before scaling and rejects a representable5e200 result. Testing only unit-scale data fails to distinguish the two algorithms. Then Handle subnormal inputs under gradual underflow and a documented flush-to-zero target. Compare results and generated instructions, then revise the admitted accuracy contract.

subtopics.title: Matrix layout, bounds and transactional output

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive the three indexing expressions and accumulator bound; prove rejection is transactional. Count arithmetic and memory traffic under the stated row-major traversal before proposing a cache model.

Implement and investigate: Implement ns_matmul(A,B,rows,inner,cols,C) for row-major int32_t arrays with each dimension1..8 and every input element in[-1024,1024]. Produce int64_t C. Reject invalid dimensions or elements before any C write; all arrays are live and disjoint. No matrix library is permitted.

Falsify and transfer: The mutant reuses column0 for every result column. Square or identity-only examples can hide layout errors; use rectangular and asymmetric values. Then Add transposed-B and blocked variants with uneven dimensions and partial tiles. Compare exact output, code size, working set and timing, including cache-warm and cache-cold runs.

subtopics.title: Saturating lanes and scalar tails

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Specify lane width, widening, alignment and disjointness. Prove the vector body and scalar tail partition [0,n), and distinguish GCC vector operators from ISO C scalar promotions.

Implement and investigate: Implement ns_add(a,b,n,out) saturating int16_t sums for n<=65535 with disjoint arrays. Widen each addition, clamp then narrow; handle every element including tails. Empty input succeeds without dereferencing arrays, invalid length fails before writes. Implement an explicit-vector adapter separately and compare it against this scalar oracle.

Falsify and transfer: The mutant rounds n down to a four-lane boundary and leaves the tail unchanged. A benchmark using only multiples of the lane count can conceal this correctness failure. Then Change lane width and input alignment; implement a runtime-dispatched path with a scalar fallback. Inspect ISA/OS feature checks, emitted instructions and equal-contract performance distributions.

subtopics.title: Accuracy admission and exceptional values

objectives.text: Derive and defend: Derive the asymmetric expected-relative policy, near-zero behavior and exceptional-value handling. Explain rounding at the acceptance boundary and why a tolerance must come from a prior requirement or error analysis.

Implement and investigate: Implement ns_close(actual,expected,atol,rtol) for finite values and finite tolerances with0<=atol and0<=rtol<=1. Use the mathematical target |actual-expected|<=atol+rtol*|expected| and define actual admission by the supplied rounded scaled comparison (boundary rounding is part of this contract), scaling to avoid overflow in difference or threshold. NaN and infinities are rejected, including equal infinities. This is an admission predicate, not proof of an algorithm error bound.

Falsify and transfer: The mutant removes the absolute component, rejecting a permitted near-zero error. Conversely a loose tolerance selected after seeing failures can hide a wrong algorithm. Then Construct condition-sensitive and metamorphic tests whose predictions do not use the implementation output as the oracle. Compare ulp-based and absolute/relative policies around subnormals, signed zero and an ill-conditioned problem.

domains.title: Error models and executable contracts
domains.depth: Mechanism implementation, falsification and independent transfer

subtopics.title: Optional and Result representations without fictitious layout guarantees

objectives.text: Derive the state cardinality of tagged versus zero-reserved optional values, including the lost present-zero state and valid result payload selection.
Implement total constructors and checked accessors while preserving output on rejected niche construction; do not copy uninitialized union members or compare padding.

Enumerate the reduced 8-bit model independently, then test actual UINT32_MAX and invalid discriminants. Measure sizeof and alignment on two available data models; a missing model is unavailable evidence. Kill premature-output-write and absence-uses-payload mutants.

Change the payload to an owning resource whose zero ID is valid. Derive an ownership-bearing tagged option and show why the old niche and byte-copy rules fail. Compare the exact documented Rust Option representation cases with this C design; no blanket ABI equivalence is allowed. Analyze void as an incomplete type with no values and _Noreturn as a function specifier. Compile a struct member of type void and an expression attempting to use a void result as a payload under strict C17 diagnostics; do not execute a falsely returning _Noreturn function. Construct a named one-state enum payload as a protocol-level unit and explain why it is not an uninhabited type or a general coercion rule.

subtopics.title: Single-evaluation propagation and atomic parser publication

objectives.text: Explain which failure stage owns the error offset, and why early-return propagation is not transaction rollback or automatic cleanup.
Implement strict checked accumulation and two single-evaluation propagation forms without statement expressions, strto* or parser libraries.

Generate all strings of length0–6 over digits0,1,9,colon,x and compare with an independent grammar/integer model. Add UINT32 bounds and long zero prefixes. Record callback/expression counters to kill double evaluation and retain a canary output for every rejection; kill premature publication and trailing-input acceptance mutants.

Replace the complete buffer with two incremental segments and preserve an explicit consumed position. Decide when an error position is absolute and when publication may occur; show a case where blindly returning the old error loses partial progress. The delayed variant adds a signed first field and forbids negative totals. Replace a proposed GNU statement-expression propagation macro with a C17 do-while statement macro taking an explicit output and goto label. Place it in an if/else and as an attempted initializer: explain why only the statement context is admitted. Count argument evaluation, test a name collision, and compare a static inline function when early return from the caller is unnecessary.

subtopics.title: Partial progress is a product, not an error alternative

objectives.text: Derive a state table in which progress and terminal/error status are independent, and distinguish accepted bytes from durable bytes.
Implement a one-call bounded adapter with overflow-free relative-to-absolute progress conversion and explicit borrowed-buffer lifetime.

Enumerate lengths0–5, valid and invalid next positions, backend counts0–6 and all status tags using a fake sink. Assert call counts, offered spans, no retry duplication and unchanged next on contract violations. Kill error-discards-progress and status-erasure mutants. Use a separate actual pipe adapter only as an additional OS experiment.

Compose with io.stream and introduce a copied bounded staging buffer. Cancellation arrives after a short write: identify what can be retried, what stays owned and what cannot be rolled back. Delayed assessment changes the sink to commit bytes in separate durable epochs.

subtopics.title: Lazy Result composition and effect-sensitive laws

objectives.text: State the preconditions for map identity/composition and and_then associativity, distinguishing pure laws from callback side effects and evaluation order.
Implement typed callback composition with one active union member, error preservation and exactly selected callback invocation.

Exhaustively compare finite pure functions on payloads0–7 using an independent table oracle. Instrument observable callbacks and construct a counterexample to a proposed optimization that eagerly evaluates an unused branch. Kill error-callback and flattened-error-loss mutants; inspect indirect-call counts before timing.

Introduce an owned payload with a destructor. Specify whether map borrows, consumes or clones; reject a design that silently duplicates ownership. Delayed assessment asks for an error-type conversion that preserves an inner cause and offset without allocation.

subtopics.title: Bounded applicative validation and transactional configuration

objectives.text: Explain why independent validation may accumulate errors while dependent checks require an admission order; define truncation independently of validity.
Implement bounded ordered diagnostics and all-or-nothing configuration publication, including structural-misuse behavior and output nonoverlap preconditions.

Enumerate boundary representatives [-1,0,1,150,151] for age, [-1,0,1024,1025] for quota and [0,1,4096,4097] for denominator across all capacities. Compare error IDs with an independent predicate list and byte/field canaries. Kill early-publication and first-error-only mutants.

Add a dependent ratio constraint quota/denominator <= limit. Explain why checking it before denominator admission would be invalid, and retain independent field diagnostics before cross-field validation. Delayed assessment requires a bounded nested path for each error and a deterministic truncation policy.

subtopics.title: Typed nonlocal-jump boundary with explicit cleanup ownership

objectives.text: Classify setjmp placement, live destination, modified automatic locals, thread identity and variably modified scope requirements from the inspected draft clauses.
Implement a bounded explicit cleanup stack and typed jump-to-result boundary without pretending that longjmp unwinds C resources.

Inject failure before and after each registration, capacity exhaustion, normal return and every admitted raised code. Count cleanup exactly once and compare reverse-order traces. Compile optimized GCC/Clang variants. Analyze deliberately invalid saved-frame and changed-local snippets without treating their execution as an oracle; kill cleanup-omission and FIFO-cleanup mutants.

Compose with a resource acquisition API that fails after the third acquisition and with T66 cleanup.scope when available. Distinguish local rollback from effects already published externally. Delayed assessment nests two separate frames and requires inner-error conversion while preserving outer cleanup order.

subtopics.title: Arithmetic policy and serial-number partial order

objectives.text: Derive the difference between mathematical range, unsigned modular semantics, saturation and the bounded-window assumption of serial comparisons.
Implement transactional policy adapters and an explicitly partial serial comparator with representable intermediate expressions.

Exhaustively enumerate an analogous 4-bit serial domain in an independent model, proving antisymmetry outside ambiguous pairs and finding nontransitive cycles. Test actual16-bit half-range neighbors and UINT32_MAX admission. Compare C17 manual checks with the separately inspected C23-draft checked arithmetic contract; kill write-before-reject and half-range-acceptance mutants.

Use the comparator in a timer queue, then change the maximum residence from less than half-range to unbounded. Supply a concrete stale/new ambiguity and repair with epochs or a wider nonwrapping lifetime contract. Delayed assessment changes the counter width and requires a fresh proof, not constant substitution alone.

subtopics.title: Contract off, observe and enforce modes with safe violation traces

objectives.text: Separate diagnostic observation, enforced rejection and C undefined behavior; explain why disabling assert can remove argument evaluation.
Implement explicit contract modes with bounded arithmetic, report-counter overflow handling and failure-side-effect accounting.

Enumerate all legal initial counters, amounts and modes against an independent integer model, checking both outputs and returned status. Compile separate assert(++counter) probes with and without NDEBUG, explaining why they are unsuitable for essential updates. Kill missing-report and enforce-still-commits mutants; the harmless attacker input is amount20 at counter90.

Replace the safe clamped teaching effect with an operation whose precondition protects memory bounds. Determine which modes may legally call it and design an admitted wrapper that stays safe even when diagnostics are off. Delayed assessment introduces concurrent report ownership and requires a new synchronization contract.

subtopics.title: Canonical rational values and the boundary of runtime refinement

objectives.text: Prove value preservation, termination and canonical representation; distinguish a runtime predicate from a static refinement type.
Implement transactional rational normalization and a validated consumer, documenting public-struct mutation and alias ownership limitations.

Enumerate numerator0–255 and denominator0–255 using Python fractions or an independently derived cross-product/gcd oracle. Test actual extrema and consecutive Fibonacci values for worst Euclid step counts. Reject unreduced-output and noncanonical-zero mutants. Verify checked consumers reject fabricated denominator0 before division.

Introduce rational addition with bounded storage. Compare rejecting intermediate overflow with cross-cancellation that admits more mathematically representable results under a declared contract. Delayed assessment changes the representation to signed numerator and requires a proof covering the minimum signed value without abs overflow.

domains.title: Ownership, lifetime and cleanup protocols
domains.depth: Mechanism construction, falsification, composition and independent transfer

subtopics.title: Owning handles and the partial-initialization frontier

objectives.text: Derive the construction frontier invariant and distinguish acquired storage, initialized object state and published ownership; compare explicit C cleanup with automatic language destruction.
Implement transactional three-resource construction and idempotent destruction using the accepted typed allocator callback ABI, proving which prefix is owned at each failure point.

Inject failure on each acquisition, reject zero and overflowing lengths before any callback, instrument release order and exactly-once counts, and test repeated destruction. Kill the omitted-rollback mutant. Extend the anchor with a callback trace that proves reverse order, not just equal release totals.

Replace the prefix with a dependency graph: acquire A, then B and C independently, then D requiring B. Write an initialized-set representation and reverse dependency cleanup. Delayed assessment makes C initialization fail after its storage acquisition; distinguish storage release from destruction of a constructed value.

subtopics.title: Scoped cleanup, conditional undo and publication by swap

objectives.text: Explain when a cleanup stack is a resource protocol, when an undo log is a semantic rollback protocol, and why neither automatically reverses already published external effects.
Implement conditional LIFO cleanup and publication-by-swap with explicit callback effects, stack capacity, transferred ownership and nonlocal-exit restrictions.

Enumerate all success/failure policy combinations through depth4 against an independent reversed-list filter, test capacity8/9 and callback reentrancy rejection, inject failure before every registration, and trace publication before old cleanup. Kill a mutant that executes every conditional cleanup.

Integrate cleanup.scope with the T65 typed jump boundary through an adapter that converts a raised error before final cleanup. Delayed assessment introduces a cleanup action that can fail: derive an explicit recovery-required result and retained owner rather than silently pretending the old void-callback contract still applies.

subtopics.title: Move protocols, source poisoning and the limits of must-use diagnostics

objectives.text: Separate ownership transfer, physical byte copying, source poisoning and diagnostic enforcement; explain why ISO C17 cannot prevent all implicit copies of this public struct.
Implement checked move/consume operations and an isolated diagnostic probe that intentionally ignores OW_MUST_USE, with extension-enabled and portable builds reported separately.

Test self-move, occupied destination, empty source, repeated consumption and allocator release counts. Reject the source-not-poisoned mutant. Compile a copied owner without consuming both copies: use it as a static counterexample, not an unbounded double-free experiment. Record whether GCC/Clang actually emit the ignored-result diagnostic.

Move a self-referential value or an inline-buffer owner: derive why copying its bytes may leave internal pointers referring to the former object. Delayed assessment hides the representation behind an opaque handle but allows duplicate handles; identify the remaining duplication attack and design checked generation/ownership tokens.

subtopics.title: Runtime borrow tracking, range splitting and finite token identities

objectives.text: Derive reader/writer interval exclusion separately from pointer lifetime, then explain finite identity exhaustion and why a runtime token does not prevent illicit raw aliases.
Implement bounded acquire/release and transactional writer splitting with arithmetic-safe extent checks, generation retirement and an explicit guard ownership rule.

Use an independent finite-set intersection oracle for all small extents/ranges/read-write combinations, then test SIZE_MAX bounds and UINT32_MAX serial retirement. Exhaust the slot table before split and compare complete pre/post books and output canaries. Kill the conflict-check omission mutant; explain that reduced exhaustive checks do not prove arbitrary C lifetimes.

Change numeric intervals into a strided view: two disjoint bounding intervals are sufficient but not necessary for disjoint element sets. Delayed assessment splits a two-dimensional tile with padding; derive exact touched indices and decide whether a conservative rejection or richer borrow representation is justified.

subtopics.title: Interior-mutability cells and guard escape boundaries
