objectives.text: Explain how dynamic borrow guards permit controlled mutation through a shared interface without making const a global immutability or thread-safety guarantee.
Implement guarded read/write and transactional replacement, composing the range guard protocol without bypassing its identity or exclusivity checks.

Test shared readers, exclusive writer, stale/released token, zero-length and partial-range tokens, failed replacement output canaries and every allowed guard-release order. Reject replacement that ignores an active guard. Analyze an escaped raw-pointer API as a contract counterexample rather than treating a clean sanitizer run as proof.

Add reentrant callbacks that read the cell while an update is in progress: choose an explicit rejection or snapshot policy and test it. Delayed assessment moves to multiple threads; derive the synchronization and guard lifetime changes rather than merely making the value atomic.

subtopics.title: Strong and weak ownership with atomic and non-atomic counts

objectives.text: Prove the distinct value/control lifetimes, no-resurrection property and count-overflow behavior; distinguish reference-count synchronization from pointee synchronization and cycle collection.

Implement strong/weak ownership twice, first under exclusion and then with C17 atomics, documenting initialization publication, owned-reference preconditions, callback effects and each memory-order edge.

Trace every strong/weak boundary with an independent counter model, test maximum-count refusal, and reject omission of the implicit weak release. Run the actual four-thread anchor, separate TSan if available, GCC/Clang optimized and ASan/UBSan builds, inspect atomic lowering and report lock-free status. A quiet race detector does not prove the memory-order argument or reclaim safety for fabricated references.

Construct a two-node strong cycle and show retained values after external owners disappear; break one edge with a weak reference and account for both control blocks. Delayed assessment races the last strong drop with weak upgrade using a synchronized start and a live weak owner: outcomes are successful ownership before destruction or DEAD, never resurrection.

subtopics.title: Copy-on-write values with transactional detach

objectives.text: Explain logical value independence, shared representation and detach cost; distinguish copy-on-write from a deep copy guarantee or automatically synchronized shared mutation.
Implement reference sharing, failure-preserving detach, unique mutation and last-owner release with explicit control-block and mutable-borrow lifetimes.

Compare every owner value to independently copied Python lists across clone/write/drop traces, inject allocation failure at each detach, test index bounds and reference overflow, and count allocations/copies for unique versus shared mutation. Reject a mutant that writes shared backing in place. Check that a borrowed mutable alias cannot legally survive cloning.

Change the backing value to contain owned resource handles whose copies can fail: derive a partial-clone frontier and rollback. Delayed assessment permits concurrent readers and one writer; define snapshot publication, reference acquisition and reclamation rather than relying on the non-atomic COW counter.

subtopics.title: Thread affinity, address pinning and asynchronous quiescence

objectives.text: Separate address-sensitive validity, thread affinity, guard permission and asynchronous reclamation; explain why checked assertions are weaker than a language pinning guarantee.
Implement the address/thread/pending state machine and an explicit io.async adapter, identifying the actual event that permits storage reuse and the lifetime of every retained address.

Enumerate submit/cancel/complete/rebind traces with output-state canaries, include duplicate events and wrong-thread calls, and reject rebinding after cancellation while pending. Use only pointers to actual live test objects. Inspect a copied self-referential record to explain why its old internal address is wrong without dereferencing a dangling pointer.

Introduce completion callbacks on a different executor: separate ownership-thread policy from completion-notification permission and queue the terminal transition safely. Delayed assessment uses a device that may still DMA after a timeout; add a RecoveryRequired/quiescence protocol and identify the physical evidence needed before reuse.

subtopics.title: Adversarial allocation through the existing typed callback ABI

objectives.text: Distinguish allocator policy, backing storage, object initialization, protocol invalidation, poison diagnostics and actual memory-safety enforcement; explain instrumentation overflow and observer effects.
Implement fail-at-N, counting and poisoning as the accepted containers.array allocator callback adapter, preserving typed storage legality and explicit finite-capacity behavior.

Sweep every allocation failure point of frontier and COW workloads, fill all eight slots, test sizes0/16/17 and counter extrema, and verify requested-prefix poison plus release accounting. Compare the imported header byte for byte with the accepted ABI and reject the no-poison mutant. Integrate with the learner dynamic array and T65 error paths, measuring actual calls rather than inferring zero allocation from source spelling.

Wrap a separately supplied upstream allocator while retaining accounting through resize success/failure; specify whether failed upstream calls consume the injection index. Delayed assessment makes an error-formatting callback allocate recursively: detect the hidden allocation and revise the whole-call-graph resource claim.

subtopics.title: A checked façade around a trusted core: bounded tenant-isolation failure

objectives.text: Derive the integer-wrap admission defect, attacker-controlled transition and exact violated authority property; distinguish a checked trusted-core boundary from whole-process memory safety.

Implement the subtraction-based boundary check, unchanged-on-failure behavior and an internal validated descriptor, preserving the simple core while documenting every remaining caller and same-process assumption.

Run the local cross-tenant demonstration with synthetic canaries, compare flawed/repaired outcomes, enumerate all ordinary tenant/offset/count combinations around8 and test UINT_MAX wrap cases. Reject the flawed-check mutant by a normal semantic assertion. Explain why ASan may remain quiet: every actual array access is in bounds. Test mitigation regression without claiming arbitrary code execution or privilege escalation.

Move the descriptor across an FFI or serialized boundary: reject fabricated fields and revalidate at that boundary rather than trusting a C typedef. Delayed assessment separates read from write capabilities and allows a read-only subview; derive authority attenuation and test that subview construction cannot widen rights.

domains.title: Algebraic data modeling and representation-safe views
domains.depth: Mechanism construction, falsification, composition and independent transfer

subtopics.title: Products, tagged sums and checked elimination

objectives.text: Derive product versus sum cardinality and distinguish a C union representation from an automatically checked discriminated union; show why -Wswitch-enum is a diagnostic policy, not an ISO C exhaustiveness theorem.

Draw all admitted tag/payload states, establish uint64 sufficiency for two uint32 values, and explain which inactive-member operations are avoided. Derive a counterexample to the claim that adding a default branch makes future variants exhaustively handled. Compare Rust enum constructors and binding behavior with C aggregate initialization and private-header discipline.

Run adt.sums and compile the missing-enumerator probe with -Wswitch-enum -Werror. Both semantic mutants must fail: omitted second product member and silently accepted invalid tag. Add every variant and invalid boundary, inspect enum size without assuming it is the wire tag size, and compare debug/release generated branches.

Add an owning text variant with a failing clone callback. Derive copy/drop/rollback and exhaustiveness obligations for every old eliminator; demonstrate which clients fail compilation and which silently preserve a default path.

subtopics.title: Newtypes and checked dimensional conversions

objectives.text: Explain why two distinct struct wrapper types reject accidental argument substitution while two typedef names for uint32_t do not; derive the exact safe seconds-to-milliseconds domain.

Derive the division-before-multiplication admission test and show that the largest accepted seconds value maps below UINT32_MAX. Compare the inspected C++ duration_cast ratio formulas; static_cast or a distinct duration type does not itself establish arbitrary destination representability. Specify round/truncate behavior before adding fractional units.

Run adt.quantities and reject wrong nominal type in a separate compilation. Kill missing-range-check and wrong-scale mutants, then test both sides of the quotient boundary. Show an explicit cast or field extraction bypass and identify programmer discipline rather than claim unforgeability.

Introduce signed microseconds and rational tick periods with a nonintegral ratio. Implement checked conversion with explicit rounding toward zero and a loss-of-precision result; derive bounds without a wider integer type.

subtopics.title: Typed flag sets and reserved-bit admission

objectives.text: Distinguish a set of independent options from a mutually exclusive sum, and explain why reserved bits must be rejected or retained under a documented evolution policy rather than silently cleared.

Define the valid mask invariant raw & ~7 ==0, all eight admitted states and ownership-free value semantics. Explain integer promotions when complementing a narrow mask; use an explicit uint32 mask. A public struct can be forged, so only constructor-admitted values have the promised invariant.

Run adt.flags; exhaustively test0..255 and each single bit position. Reject the silent-mask mutant and empty-set rejection mutant. Show a newly reserved bit cannot be accidentally converted into success by masking.

Negotiate separate required and advisory bit sets between two schema versions. Preserve unknown advisory bits for forwarding while rejecting unsupported required bits, and prove the union operation cannot manufacture support.

subtopics.title: UTF-8 smart constructors and validated borrowed text

objectives.text: Derive a UTF-8 validation predicate from RFC3629 and explain why successful construction proves byte encoding only while the backing bytes remain live and unchanged.

Track input position and remaining continuation count without forming an out-of-range pointer. For each sequence derive minimum scalar value and maximum scalar value; compare scalar count with byte count. State storage lifetime and mutation restrictions explicitly, including a safe constructed example where another alias changes a previously validated buffer.

Run adt.text and the Python strict UTF-8 differential oracle for all one/two-byte strings plus specified three/four-byte boundary samples. Kill overlong and surrogate acceptance mutants. Record that Python decoding is an independent implementation, not a proof of normalization or all higher-level text properties.

Add an incremental decoder across chunks with at most3retained bytes and finalization. Test every split of each boundary sequence, cancellation that drops pending bytes, and a copying owner that can preserve validation under caller mutation.

subtopics.title: Branded pool handles with checked generations

objectives.text: Separate nominal handle category, pool identity, slot generation and ownership; demonstrate why a C wrapper cannot create a compile-time fresh brand per runtime pool or enforce linear use.

Derive FREE/LIVE/RETIRED transitions and count available slots. Explain why copying a handle is permitted by C yet does not duplicate ownership. Pool objects must remain live at fixed addresses and cannot be reinitialized or reused while handles survive: pointer identity does not prevent ABA across object lifetimes. Compare PhantomData nominal/lifetime roles without claiming equivalent static checks.

Run adt.brands and enumerate short acquire/release/get traces against an independent occupancy/generation model. Kill owner-check omission and generation-check omission independently. Compile a wrong-category handle probe; show that copying or explicitly constructing a valid public representation bypasses any unforgeability claim.

Replace the owner pointer with a nonreused externally assigned pool identity and implement relocation of the pool. Then introduce concurrent get/release: provide a reclamation/lifetime protocol, not just an atomic generation counter.

subtopics.title: Read-only strided views and ownership boundaries

objectives.text: Derive required backing extent from shape and strides, including empty shapes and overflow, and distinguish a read-only overlapping view from a mutable injective layout.

Prove multiplication and addition guards before computing the last element offset; explain why logical element count need not equal required span. Compare span contiguous access and mdspan layout_stride preconditions. Define when two logical indices alias and why a writable transfer needs stronger validation or an explicit alias contract.

Run adt.views; enumerate small shapes/strides/capacities against a Python coordinate-set oracle. Kill row-major-assumption and missing-capacity-admission mutants. Audit zero/SIZE_MAX boundaries and distinguish arithmetic acceptance from existence of a real caller object of that extent.

Implement mutable transpose/submatrix views and a SIMD reduction adapter. Establish injectivity or documented repeated-write semantics, equivalent overflow/alias contracts, and measure scalar/vector behavior only on admitted layouts.

subtopics.title: Recursive arena values and typed indices

objectives.text: Derive acyclicity from a topological child-index invariant and explain when a checked arena can support unchecked internal traversal without allowing later mutation to invalidate the proof.

Prove by induction on node index that each value is available before its parent; separate index category from actual range validity. Give O(count)time/O(32)stack and compare a recursive tree that duplicates shared children. For validate-once extension, make the arena immutable or invalidate its certificate after every structural mutation.

Run adt.arena and independent postfix/tree evaluation cases. Kill forward-reference acceptance and arithmetic-overflow omission. Add unreachable malformed nodes, multiple roots, shared children, empty and maximum count, then record stack-use output.

Support bounded cyclic graphs for a monotone dataflow analysis. Replace topological induction with a lattice/worklist convergence argument and distinguish no fixed point, insufficient iteration budget and successful convergence.

subtopics.title: Lenses and prisms with falsifiable laws

objectives.text: Derive lens get-put, put-get and put-put laws and prism review/preview round trips; explain how lawful optics differ from arbitrary field mutation helpers.

Write each law as an executable predicate and derive which information an update may change. Compare the C functions with the inspected lens type laws; C types do not enforce those laws. Distinguish field equality from raw struct memcmp because padding need not encode semantic identity.

Run adt.optics:256combinations assess get-put/put-get/put-put and prism round trips. Kill the collateral-y-write and EMPTY-as-NUMBER mutants. Add composition of nested pairs, identify a law violated by a clamping setter, and explain why exhaustive small domains are not proof for arbitrary callback optics.

Implement a lens into an optional nested configuration and a prism for a versioned error sum. Decide which updates are partial, state revised laws, and produce counterexamples to importing total-lens laws unchanged.

subtopics.title: Evolution-aware sums and lossless tolerant readers

objectives.text: Distinguish tolerance from permissiveness: an unknown noncritical alternative can be retained exactly, while malformed known alternatives and unknown required semantics must fail.

Define a sum of known-number, known-empty and unknown bytes; retain tag and payload even when semantics are unavailable. State lifetime, disjointness, maximum255payloadbytes and overflow-free size calculation. Compare binary unknown-field preservation with the inspected Protobuf guide and demonstrate a field-wise rebuilding path that loses unknown data.

Run adt.evolution and construct a two-version relay trace. Kill unknown-payload-discard and malformed-known-acceptance mutants. Test all truncation points, trailing bytes, capacity shortages, zero-length unknown payload and borrowed-buffer mutation. Record which operations preserve unknown data and which deliberately reject it.

Add duplicate fields and canonical ordering to an extensible record format. Specify how unknown duplicates participate in signatures and forwarding, and demonstrate why accepting arbitrary unknown fields can violate a higher-level security policy.

subtopics.title: Zero-copy packet view with precise error sum

objectives.text: Port the supplied census packet-view artifact to C while preserving its admitted wire states, error distinctions and borrowed-payload lifetime; identify guarantees supplied by the C API versus the compared language wrappers.

Derive a state table for every failure stage and prove length-3 subtraction is reached only after header validation. No struct overlay, unaligned integer load, allocation or payload copy is permitted. Compare C tag/error conventions with census C++ variant/expected/span without treating the example as an authoritative language specification.

Run adt.packet and enumerate header/extent/tag combinations against the independent byte parser. Kill trailing-byte acceptance and nonempty-ack acceptance separately. Test all truncations and prior-output preservation, then integrate actual learner io.frame and bytes.cursor artifacts with recorded source identities. Public direct-parser anchors do not establish that integration.

Add segmented zero-copy payloads from a receive ring with wraparound and a retained borrow token. Prove storage cannot be recycled while a consumer holds the packet; compare copying and borrowing under equivalent release/cancellation semantics.

domains.title: Metaprogramming, reflection and law-driven generation
domains.depth: Mechanism construction, falsification, composition and independent transfer

subtopics.title: Template-header monomorphization and associated types

objectives.text: Explain how repeated template-header inclusion generates distinct typed functions, how associated element/ring types must agree, and why token substitution has no trait-implementation proof or automatic instantiation isolation.

Derive head<count/capacity invariants, occupied logical slots and output ownership. Compare generated specialization with Rust generic/associated-type obligations and show a mismatched ring/element instantiation diagnosed by C. Explain why a template include guard would silently suppress the second instantiation and why internal macro names can collide.

Run metaprog.mono and inspect preprocessed two-instance source. Kill incorrect-tail-index and stationary-head mutants. Compile and link two translation units using declarations to detect accidental multiple definitions; record generated symbol count and text size separately from handwritten equivalents under the same capacity/failure contract.

Instantiate a ring of owning objects with fallible clone/drop callbacks. Derive rollback on failed push and destruction order on clear; compare monomorphized and erased implementations with equal semantics and measured code growth.

subtopics.title: Constraint probes and constant storage parameters

objectives.text: Separate a required C constraint diagnostic, a chosen -Werror rejection, and a runtime range guard; show which properties constant-size generic storage can check before execution.

Derive count<=SIZE_MAX/width before multiplication and the independent budget bound. Explain why C17 _Static_assert requires an integer constant expression, VLA support differs from fixed arrays, and syntactically valid macros do not impose an abstract trait. Compare the inspected Rust const-generic type/use restrictions without claiming arbitrary compile-time evaluation equivalence.

Run metaprog.constraints and compile the negative constraint probes expecting a named diagnostic, not a link failure. Kill multiplication-overflow omission and storage-budget omission independently. Test size_t-width changes analytically and inspect whether published C23 wording is available before attributing a C2x compiler behavior to the standard.

Support a compile-time power-of-two ring capacity and a runtime fallback. Derive which optimization can use masking, reject an invalid constant capacity, and ensure a nonconstant caller cannot bypass runtime validation.

subtopics.title: Policy composition with explicit failure semantics

objectives.text: Explain how a policy changes the operation contract and therefore the permitted performance comparison; distinguish compile-time specialization from runtime policy dispatch.

Prove value<=limit before subtracting limit-value, and define how a single input greater thanlimit is handled. Inputs/outputs are disjoint. State no allocation, single-threaded execution and failure publication at the end. Compare a policy parameter with Rust const parameters/trait-associated behavior only at the documented boundary.

Run metaprog.policies and inject every prefix crossing the limit. Kill accidental-saturation-for-rejection and wrong-empty-identity mutants. Inspect specialized and dynamic assembly and benchmark only comparisons preserving the same overflow and empty-input contracts.

Compose reduction with a caller-defined projection and fallible element acquisition. Specify evaluation order, callback side effects, rollback limits and whether saturation may short-circuit without skipping required effects.

subtopics.title: Portable C17 variadic machinery and single evaluation

objectives.text: Derive a bounded1..4argument dispatch macro without __VA_OPT__ or GNU comma deletion, and distinguish single evaluation from the unspecified order of function arguments.

Show token substitution, rescan, selector position and parentheses for each admitted arity. Explain why an empty token argument differs from omitted variadic arguments in C17, and why this lab deliberately has a distinct zero-argument entry. Compare N3033 proposal semantics without presenting a proposal as the inspected final C23 standard.

Run metaprog.variadic, inspect -E output, and compile strict C17 probes. Kill duplicate-evaluation and incorrect-zero-identity mutants. Add arguments with commas protected by parentheses and demonstrate an unsafe unparenthesized form in a diagnostic-only target; retain a separate C2x __VA_OPT__ observation.

Build a bounded logging dispatcher that optionally attaches source metadata, with a distinct zero-field operation. Preserve single evaluation and type checking while making expansion limits explicit; diagnose unsupported arity without compiler-specific comma extensions.

subtopics.title: Generic customization with cv-preserving receivers

objectives.text: Explain why selecting a function designator with _Generic and calling it afterward preserves typed receiver checking, while invalid unselected expressions can still require diagnostics.

Distinguish top-level pointer qualifiers from pointed-to const and state the compatible-type association restrictions. The controlling expression is not evaluated; only the selected call argument is evaluated. Explain why the generic selection should choose valid function names rather than embed branch-specific invalid field operations.

Run metaprog.generic and compile unsupported-type/const-write diagnostic probes. Kill const-receiver-policy substitution and extra controlling-expression evaluation mutants. Check GCC and Clang with C17, and record implementation differences involving top-level qualifiers as observations requiring precise source interpretation.

Add volatile device-view receivers through explicit APIs. Separate permitted volatile access, side effects and ordering from constness; inspect emitted accesses and avoid claiming that volatile supplies synchronization or device barriers.

subtopics.title: Single-source field reflection and explicit wire operations

objectives.text: Derive declarations, field names, offsets and wire operations from one authoritative field list without confusing implementation layout reflection with a portable serialization format.

Explain stringification/token substitution and why the field list is a local schema, not arbitrary introspection of undeclared C types. Distinguish native field offset, native sizeof, wire width and schema identity. Compare the declared generated interface with language macro/derive facilities; no C++26 reflection claim is inferred without inspected final specification.

Run metaprog.reflection and regenerate a changed schema in a temporary workspace. Kill endian reversal and missing-field-descriptor mutants. Compile under altered packing/alignment only as an implementation-specific comparison and retain canonical wire bytes unchanged.

Add an optional tagged field and derive decode, equality, validation and visitor operations. Define migration/version rules and demonstrate a stale generated consumer that still compiles; design a build-time schema fingerprint check that catches it.

subtopics.title: Derived equality, hashing and shrinking law counterexamples

objectives.text: Explain the equality-implies-equal-hash law, why cached/nonsemantic fields must be excluded consistently, and what deterministic generation plus shrinking establishes and leaves unproved.

Prove reflexivity/symmetry/transitivity obligations separately from hashing and collisions. Specify FNV parameters and unsigned64 wrap; this is not a cryptographic integrity claim. The shrinking order finds a local minimum under decrement moves, not necessarily a globally simplest witness for arbitrary nonmonotone predicates. Callback/context must remain live, deterministic and side-effect controlled.

Run metaprog.laws, independently recompute canonical hashes and enumerate bounded law triples. Kill equality-ignores-y and hash-includes-cache mutants. Inject a deliberately wrong equality/hash callback through the learner testing.faults adapter and retain a minimized witness; explain why equal hashes do not imply equal keys.

Add an allocation-failing string owner and generators for operation traces. Shrink while preserving preconditions and the same failure class; compare bytewise, semantic and normalized-text equality contracts before deriving hashes.

subtopics.title: Typed formatting and transactional bounded sinks

objectives.text: Distinguish compile-time argument-category checking from compile-time parsing of an arbitrary format string, and prove bounded sink failure does not publish partial output.

Derive the10digit bound for UINT32_MAX and reverse temporary digits only after capacity admission. For text, prove scan stops on insufficient capacity without publishing a prefix. Compare C++ basic_format_string constant-evaluation compatibility with this narrower C factory: it enforces argument categories, not arbitrary formatting grammar or backing lifetime.

Run metaprog.formatting, compile an unsupported MP_ARG category probe, and test every capacity0..11. Kill failure-used-count modification and zero-as-empty-output mutants. Compare against an independent decimal-string oracle and a guard-filled output suffix; distinguish valid text termination preconditions from bound checking.

Add a parsed format DSL with typed placeholder descriptors and partial streaming sinks. Specify format validation separately from argument typing, and make partial writes/retry offsets explicit rather than silently keeping the transactional API promise.

subtopics.title: A bounded hygienic token expander written in C

objectives.text: Explain variable capture using symbol identity plus syntax context, and distinguish preserving call-site argument context from assigning a fresh context to introduced bindings.

Define identifier equality as(symbol,context), track binding/reference identities through an expansion, and show how call-site symbol7/context5 remains distinct from introducedsymbol7/context12. Explain nested expansion context retention and finite namespace exhaustion. Compare the inspected Rust mixed-site hygiene rules precisely; the model uses an explicit stronger uniform context scheme for introduced names.

Run metaprog.hygiene and compare against an independent token/context transformer. Kill retagged-call-site-argument and wrapping-context mutants. Build a tiny environment resolver to demonstrate harmless capture: the flawed output resolves the argument to the introduced synthetic binding instead of its caller binding. Retain corrected and flawed token traces.

Add nested macros, repetition with equal-length metavariables and a depth/token expansion budget. Specify intentional capture escapes explicitly, prove budget consumption, and distinguish nontermination prevention from complete macro-language equivalence.

subtopics.title: Declarative build graphs and deterministic table generation

objectives.text: Derive build ordering separately from action invalidation, identify hidden inputs, and explain why a content key is only as complete and collision-resistant as its declared input model.

Prove Kahn-style readiness and termination, show how dependency content propagates into consumers, and distinguish source identity from timestamp ordering. Compare Ninja explicit/implicit/order-only dependency semantics and command-line rebuild tracking. The educational FNV key is not collision-resistant; require full input equality or a suitable cryptographic digest before any untrusted shared cache use.

Run metaprog.buildgraph and independent Python topological/hash reconstruction. Kill omitted-configuration and omitted-dependency-key mutants. Compile/run the generated C table consumer, permute input storage without changing logical IDs, and inject a missing implicit dependency to demonstrate stale generated metadata.

Introduce an incremental cache with toolchain, environment, include-file and schema dependencies. Simulate crashes during artifact publication and hash collisions; define atomic replacement and full-input verification. Compare a parallel scheduler only after establishing dependency and output ownership.

domains.title: Dispatch, closures and type erasure
domains.depth: Mechanism implementation, lifetime analysis, falsification and independent transfer

subtopics.title: Named interfaces, structural probes and semantic conformance

objectives.text: Distinguish nominal registration, structural syntax compatibility and semantic interface laws; explain which C function-pointer mismatches need diagnostics and which wrong implementations still type-check.
Implement typed view constructors and a checked erased call wrapper with exactly-once callback invocation, stable table lifetime and failure-output staging.
Generate values and error callbacks against an independent direct-call model, reject incompatible signature/receiver translations and kill status-erasure and wrong-result mutants.

Transfer to an interface with two mutually constrained operations such as length and copy. Construct a table that satisfies every signature but violates their relation; assess the relation separately. Compare named Rust impl conformance with the C registration and explain why free C functions do not add language extension-method lookup.

subtopics.title: Fat views, embedded tables and unsafe qualifier substitution

objectives.text: Derive the two representations and their table/data lifetime and cache costs; distinguish logical two-part dispatch from an ABI promise of exactly two machine words.
Implement an embedded-to-view adapter preserving concrete receiver address, const access and failure publication.

Validate both representations against the same direct implementation and compile the double-pointer qualifier counterexample under strict C17; diagnose why one-level qualifier addition does not generalize recursively.

Compare Rust trait-object representation and lifetime bounds with the C pair, then change to a borrowed subobject and multiple interfaces. Recompute pointer adjustment, owner storage and invalidation; no automatic variance or lifetime proof is inherited. Compile the supplied empty-struct probe under strict C17 and compare a one-byte marker field with the inspected Rust zero-sized marker rules. Record extension diagnostics and actual size separately; no zero-size or no-cost C guarantee follows.

subtopics.title: Dictionary passing, specialization and effect-sensitive folds

objectives.text: Derive the dictionary as explicit operation evidence and state the laws required before reordering or parallelizing a fold.
Implement dictionary and specialized forms with identical admission, prefix-overflow and output contracts, maintaining callback order and count.
Exhaust length0–5 over values{-2,0,3} against an independent mathematical fold and failure trace; kill swapped-operand and partial-publication mutants.

Measure code size, indirect branches, compilation and inlining under fixed versus runtime-selected dictionaries. Explain why a C macro over concrete types or void-pointer dictionary does not implement Haskell kind checking over a type constructor; give a rejected or unchecked encoding counterexample.

subtopics.title: Capture ownership and shared, mutable, consuming invocation

objectives.text: Separate capture-by-value/reference from invocation capabilities and explain the documented Rust rule that move capture alone does not imply only FnOnce.
Implement the three explicit modes with checked arithmetic, exactly-once consumption and clear borrowed/owned capture lifetimes; add borrowed-slice and owning-resource closures.

Enumerate operation sequences including repeated calls, failed calls, reinitialization under its ownership precondition and copied-state misuse; compare state transitions with an independent finite model.

Transfer to a retained asynchronous callback. Establish an environment outlives relation, cancellation ownership and reentrancy policy; show how copying an active C struct defeats a local consumed bit even when every ordinary call checks it.

subtopics.title: Owning erased calls over the byte-only small buffer

objectives.text: Derive erased-call representation, invocation thunk, ownership and empty states; distinguish byte encoding from placing an arbitrary typed object in character storage.
Implement capture construction, explicit movement and no-fail destruction through dod.small_buffer with no duplicated allocator logic, including a spill and failure rollback.
Inject each allocation/codec failure, test source/destination/self move and repeated drop, and verify exactly-once external destruction plus unchanged outputs on failing calls.

Compare owning C erasure, a borrowed function reference and the documented C++ move_only_function/function_ref contracts. Analyze inline storage, movement constraints and empty invocation without claiming common ABI or universal small-buffer capacity.

Transfer to a self-referential or over-aligned capture and a callback returning a borrowed reference. Either provide a justified typed representation/relocator/lifetime protocol or reject it explicitly; a byte copy is not a general solution.

subtopics.title: Ordered multiple dispatch and cache invalidation epochs

objectives.text: Derive ordered dispatch keys, missing-method behavior, cache coherence and epoch exhaustion; distinguish explicit symmetry from accidental argument normalization.
Implement registration and cached invocation preserving output on failure; add a two-entry policy with an explicit eviction rule.
Enumerate all nine type pairs and registration/cache histories, including cached misses, replacement/removal and epoch exhaustion; kill stale-epoch and reversed-pair mutants.

Transfer to subtype fallback with two equally specific candidates. Define ambiguity detection and coherence before caching, then compare lookup, code size and update costs under monomorphic and varied call traces.

subtopics.title: Intrusive membership, initial-member recovery and external behavior

objectives.text: Prove circular forward/backward invariants, single membership and item/list lifetime; explain why the sentinel is not a DSItem.
Implement bounded insertion/removal and checked traversal using the inspected first-member conversion rule; attach external behavior without assuming an object hierarchy.
Enumerate insertion/removal permutations and wrong-list operations, recompute both directions independently and reject omitted-backlink and duplicate-membership mutants.

Transfer to an object with two intrusive hooks and movable surrounding storage. Compare an explicit parent pointer, typed index and platform-specific container recovery; define every invalidation rule and inspect generated code/diagnostics without executing an invalid cast.

subtopics.title: Opaque modules with explicit service injection and failure effects

objectives.text: Derive public incomplete-type opacity and dependency ownership; distinguish hidden representation, nominal type identity and an unforgeable security boundary.
Implement a bounded factory, close protocol and injected-service operation with atomic result publication and explicit irreversible callback effects.
Inject failures at each service invocation and exhaust the factory; compile a client attempting private-field access and compare two implementations through one independent contract suite.

Transfer to a parameterized module with correlated key/value types. Explain which relations a typed C facade can enforce and which erased dictionary cannot; compare fixed opaque concrete return identity with runtime existential selection and state why neither is reproduced merely by returning void*.

subtopics.title: Authority attenuation, revocation and the limits of C tokens

objectives.text: State the authority graph, permitted attacker actions and property: delegated rights remain a subset and revoked epochs cannot authorize a new effect. Distinguish a cooperative token from an unforgeable capability.
Implement subset admission, owner/epoch validation, bounded revocation and checked effect publication without global ambient authority.
Enumerate all rights masks, owner pairs and epoch transitions; demonstrate harmless unauthorized-counter change in the two explicit mutants and regression rejection in the repair.

Transfer to delegation across an actual process boundary with opaque server-side IDs. Define authentication, replay, ID reuse, revocation and confused-deputy behavior, and show why a hidden C struct alone does not solve arbitrary in-process writes.

subtopics.title: Versioned plugin objects and borrowed code lifetime

objectives.text: Separate ISO object/function pointer rules, the target ABI and Linux loader semantics, including dlsym error handling, constructor effects and logical invalidation after close.

Implement failure-clean loading, exact version/size admission and borrowed-code quiescence using a typed exported object; define trusted fixture extent rather than pretending a size field proves memory validity.

Run original good/bad/missing-symbol/size fixtures under GCC/Clang sanitizers, verify each acquisition prefix and reject ignored-version and premature-close mutants by intended assertions before an invalid call.

Transfer to an ABI with optional trailing methods and independently built clients. Specify common-prefix compatibility, alignment/calling-convention/version negotiation and code/data allocator ownership; test with separate shared libraries and record unsupported ABI combinations.

subtopics.title: Quiescent hot reload with staged state handoff and retirement

objectives.text: Derive prepare/commit/retire states and the quiescence condition covering every borrowed code/data pointer; distinguish rejected migration from committed reload with pending cleanup.
Implement staged migration, source ownership consumption, finite generations and explicit retired collection, preserving the old service on every precommit failure.
Explore reload/borrow/release/collect/fail sequences against an independent ownership/state model, verifying no duplicated or lost handle and no state publication before migration succeeds.

Transfer to asynchronous plugin callbacks and owned variable-size state. Define snapshot/serialization, cancellation acknowledgement, allocator boundaries and bounded retirement; measure pause time and retained resources without claiming transparent live-code replacement.

domains.title: Data-oriented layout and persistent structures
domains.depth: Implementation, falsification, resource analysis and independent transfer

subtopics.title: Hot and cold columns with transactional numeric updates

objectives.text: Derive AoS and SoA address/traffic models for a position-only update and a whole-record consumer, including padding, cache-line assumptions and the different identity of a record after splitting fields.
Implement a staged SoA update and an equal-contract AoS version generated from a shared field list; distinguish token-driven generation from runtime or language reflection.
Enumerate small signed input products and all failing record positions with an independent integer oracle; verify untouched columns and kill skipped-update and premature-prefix-commit mutants.

Measure warmed and cold working sets, vectorization reports, code size and conversion costs under equal overflow semantics. Report crossover uncertainty; demonstrate a whole-record workload where SoA can lose.

Transfer to an array-of-small-tiles layout with an optional cold column. Derive row/column bounds and schema evolution before changing the implementation; C diagnostics do not verify field-list semantic consistency.

subtopics.title: Inline bytes, allocator failure and explicit relocation

objectives.text: Derive the representation invariant for empty, inline and heap states and the exact invalidation events for borrowed views; explain why alignment of a character array alone does not permit arbitrary typed C objects.
Implement all capacity transitions and a fixed-capacity alternative using allocator injection, with strong append rejection and exactly-once resource release under move/reset.

Inject every allocation failure and test capacity16/17, maximum128, zero append, self move, nonempty destination, repeated reset and compact after truncation; compare byte sequences with an independent list model.

Compare the documented LLVM inline-vector idea with this C byte representation and a typed-union alternative. Measure owner footprint, allocations, copy traffic and spill hysteresis rather than claiming universal zero overhead.

Integrate dod.small_buffer with an erased closure byte capture: define which values can be encoded, which callbacks own external resources and why memcpy of a self-referential capture is not relocation.

subtopics.title: Four saturating byte lanes without cross-lane carries

objectives.text: Derive low7-bit addition, high-bit combination and saturation masks, proving which intermediate carries can occur and why neighboring lanes remain independent.
Implement the unsigned SWAR expression and an independent scalar oracle without relying on char signedness, endian memory reinterpretation or vector extensions.
Exhaust all65,536 lane input pairs in every position and with neighboring boundary lanes, then add deterministic mixed-lane random words; kill ordinary packed-add and inverted-overflow-mask mutants.

Compare scalar and SWAR code under equal saturation semantics at multiple optimization levels, checking generated instructions and a changed16-bit-lane derivation. Distinguish source-level branchlessness from timing guarantees and ISA support.

subtopics.title: Stable typed slots, dense iteration and finite identity

objectives.text: Prove both directions of the dense/rank bijection and distinguish stable address, stable logical identity, stable iteration order and owner lifetime.
Implement swap-erased dense IDs with typed slot storage, generation admission and retirement; implement a two-page extension without moving live payload objects.
Explore all add/remove sequences up to length7 over four IDs against an independent live-set model, checking stale and foreign-owner handles, last-row removal and pool exhaustion.

Transfer to a payload owning a resource and a consumer holding a raw pointer. Define destruction and invalidation, then show why generation checks do not revoke that pointer or authorize concurrent reclamation.

subtopics.title: Archetype migration with capacity admission and row repair

objectives.text: Derive entity-to-table/row and table-row-to-entity invariants, query mask semantics and the distinction between stable entity ID and invalidated row references.

Implement migration with destination admission before source removal, swap-row repair and transactional query updates; implement required/excluded-mask query selection and versioned cache invalidation.
Enumerate create/migrate/update sequences against an independent per-entity dictionary, inject destination-full and arithmetic rejection, and diagnose lost-entity and stale-row-map mutants.

Compare sparse-set and archetype storage under query-heavy and mutation-heavy workloads, including migration copies, cache maintenance and iterator invalidation. Compose with typed stable handles under a changed deletion/reuse policy.

subtopics.title: Path copying, zipper contexts and retained-version costs

objectives.text: Derive persistence as multiple observable versions with shared immutable subgraphs, distinguishing it from durable storage and from a mutable object with a const pointer.
Implement leaf-to-root path copying, an explicit zipper reconstruction and failure rollback without mutating published nodes; state allocator ownership and snapshot lifetime.
Inject failure at every cloned-node ordinal, compare all8 cells of every retained root with independent array snapshots, and recompute reachability and sharing from roots.

Analyze fresh-node work, retained-node space, stack depth and region reclamation latency; implement a bounded reference-count alternative with exactly-once reclamation for a shared child and explain why it is not concurrent safe by itself.

Transfer to a tree with owned string leaves and a clone callback that can fail. Define rollback for already cloned resources and compare the documented persistent-collection Clone requirement with C programmer discipline.

subtopics.title: Bitmap rank, full-hash collisions and persistent map updates

objectives.text: Derive bitmap rank as the population count of preceding bits and prove compact-child count/order invariants; distinguish trie-prefix, full-hash and actual-key equality.
Implement lookup/update with collision buckets and path copying, then deletion with defined empty-node normalization and immutable prior snapshots.
Exhaust keys0–31 and insertion/deletion permutations for collision pairs and differing bitmap positions; compare each version with an independent dictionary and inject every clone failure.

Analyze hash quality, collision-bucket growth, retained versions and pointer/bitmap costs under equal contracts. Transfer to an attacker-selected constant hash and specify bounded denial-of-service behavior without claiming constant worst-case lookup.

subtopics.title: Shared text DAGs, editing alternatives and coordinate meaning

objectives.text: Prove ordered-DAG sequence semantics, cached length consistency and ownership of shared leaves; distinguish byte, codepoint, grapheme and line coordinates.
Implement transactional leaf/concat/flatten and byte-index/split operations, including empty boundaries and shared subgraphs without cycles.
Implement gap-buffer and piece-table editing with complete capacity and source-lifetime contracts; drive identical insert/delete scripts through all representations and an independent flat oracle.

Investigate chain depth, rebalancing, fragmentation and retained backing storage using adversarial concatenation and edit locality; derive a balance criterion from the inspected rope paper without importing its measurements as this lab results.

Transfer to UTF-8 scalar-index edits and invalid byte sequences. Define validation, coordinate conversion and snapshot ownership, then demonstrate a case where byte equality alone does not establish the requested text operation.

domains.title: Typestate, protocols and state machines
domains.depth: Mechanism construction, experimental falsification and independent transfer

subtopics.title: Consuming typestate and explicit recovery after partial device writes

objectives.text: Derive a lifecycle transition table including partially configured RecoveryRequired, token generation retirement and storage lifetime; distinguish C wrapper diagnostics from Rust moves.

Implement pt_device_init/configure/close/recover with consumed matching tokens, unchanged success-output on failure, and externally certified quiescence before cleanup. Fail after each of the two control writes.

Enumerate failure stage0/1/2, quiet0/1, copied stale tokens and UINT32_MAX retirement; compile the wrong-wrapper fixture and demonstrate that a copied correct wrapper still compiles. Reject false-CLOSED and ignored-generation mutants.

Replace one synchronous control write with deferred DMA completion. Design an owning Recovery token that retains a buffer until quiescence, including reset while a stale alias survives; explain why generation checks cannot inspect a dangling pointer safely.

subtopics.title: Staged builders, presence masks and cross-field admission

objectives.text: Separate required-field presence from value validity and cross-field constraints; identify what staged C wrapper types can diagnose and what a public struct can bypass.

Implement one-shot setters and atomic finish for address, length and timeout using the exact bounds in CONTRACTS.md, and construct a second staged-wrapper interface with the same admitted configurations.

Enumerate all eight presence masks, every setter permutation, duplicate setters, alignment violations and the address+length boundary. Preserve output canaries on incomplete/invalid finish; reject omitted-mask and omitted-cross-field-check mutants.

Add a mutually exclusive DMA or polling mode where DMA requires alignment and polling forbids a callback. Derive the new state space and compare type proliferation with a checked sum representation; the delayed variant permits safe replacement of one previously set field.

subtopics.title: Dual binary session automata with bounded dialogue

objectives.text: Derive dual send/receive traces for HELLO, ACCEPT, a bounded DATA/ACK loop and BYE; distinguish runtime protocol conformance from transport liveness and language-enforced session types.

Implement pt_session_step for both roles, phase and remaining count, rejecting wrong direction/tag and terminal reuse without progress. Build an in-process two-endpoint trace driver using only synthetic messages.

Enumerate both roles, remaining0..8 and every phase/tag/direction, compare against a separately written transition table and assert rejected-state preservation. Reject direction-erasure and ACK-does-not-decrement mutants.

Introduce a choice between retryable rejection and cancellation, plus a peer crash between DATA and ACK. Specify which endpoint detects failure and whether a consumed message can be replayed; compare with the explicitly scoped guarantees of Sesh.

subtopics.title: Hierarchical run-to-completion transitions and observable entry order

objectives.text: Derive least-common-ancestor exit/entry paths, inherited FAIL handling, external self transitions and internal PING; distinguish this bounded HSM subset from full UML semantics.
Implement pt_dispatch with inner-first exits, outer-first entries, a nonreentry guard, and transactional trace-capacity failure. Produce a table-driven independent transition oracle.

Check every active leaf/event pair, insufficient trace capacity, repeated BUSY START and PING exhaustion. Reject reversed-entry and omitted-exit mutants; compare exact action sequences rather than final states alone.

Add an entry action that posts another event and a guard on the parent transition. Queue the posted event until the current run-to-completion step ends and define guard fallback; the delayed variant introduces a local transition that intentionally preserves a composite state.

subtopics.title: Bounded active-object queue and failure-preserving dispatch

objectives.text: Explain serialized event ownership, run-to-completion scheduling and the difference between event admission and successful handling in an MCU active object.

Compose the HSM with a four-slot copied-event ring; reject overflow unchanged and retain an event whose dispatch fails. Integrate learner-owned execution.tasks and sync.copied_queue through an explicit adapter.

Test full/empty/wraparound, trace-capacity failure before removal and bursts CONNECT/START/FINISH/FAIL. Reject overwrite-on-full and consume-before-dispatch-success mutants. Model adversarial event floods using synthetic counters.

Change one producer to an interrupt source and two consumers to competing tasks. Identify the single-consumer assumption that fails, implement a bounded enqueue synchronization adapter, and choose a documented policy for an unhandled event that blocks the queue.

subtopics.title: Stackless resumable functions with persistent explicit state

objectives.text: Explain switch-based continuation labels, automatic-local lifetimes, duplicate-label constraints and why suspension across an ordinary function return does not retain a C stack.
Implement the three-value checked summation frame and a PT_BEGIN/WAIT/END version; store every value live across suspension in the frame and reserve label0 and UINT32_MAX.

Exercise unavailable input between every accepted value, overflow with unchanged state, stable DONE and distinct interleaved frames. Compile duplicate-label and wrong-scope proposals as diagnostic/analysis cases; reject reset-sum and unchecked-overflow mutants.

Turn the sum into a cancellable framed decoder that owns a partially initialized buffer, then compose two waiting child functions. Compare the explicit subframe requirement with actual stackful fibers; delayed assessment adds a timeout that races the third value.

subtopics.title: Memory behavior trees, running-child ownership and abort

objectives.text: Derive the different control rules of sequence and selector nodes, and distinguish a memory tree from a reactive tree that rechecks earlier guards.
Implement bounded validated node traversal, per-composite cursors, running-leaf ownership bits and exactly-once abort on cancellation, with a callback-reentry guard.

Use a leaf trace where the first child succeeds and the second remains RUNNING over repeated ticks; verify the first effect is not repeated. Check invalid topology, nested sequence/selector, reentry and cancellation twice. Reject cursor-reset and omitted-abort mutants.

Introduce a reactive safety guard that can invalidate a running action. Specify which subtree is aborted before reevaluation, which completed effects cannot be undone, and whether callback failure provides strong or basic recovery; delayed assessment adds shared subtrees and forces a new ownership representation.

subtopics.title: Typestate firmware driver with uncertain DMA ownership

objectives.text: Separate start failure, cancellation intent, hardware quiescence and buffer reuse; identify the trusted adapter facts needed to release an asynchronous loan.

Implement pt_driver_start/complete/recover over the supplied original register/DMA model, retaining buffers on partial start failure. Connect all specified firmware_io and task/queue imports in a source-bound adapter integration.

Inject start failure after the model retains a buffer, repeated failed quiescence, successful recovery, completion with quiet0 and duplicate completion. Count watchdog and release events; reject premature-release and quiet-check omission mutants.

Compose UART transmission, timer deadline and DMA completion across a reset. Preserve the loan until the new hardware epoch is proven quiescent, and redesign generation issuance when wrap or stale interrupts are possible; delayed assessment changes DMA to noncoherent cached memory.

domains.title: Iterators, coroutines and continuations
domains.depth: Mechanism construction, experimental falsification and independent transfer

subtopics.title: Lazy fused pull pipelines and typed early termination

objectives.text: Derive evaluation order, consumption and side effects for filter-even/map-square/take, and distinguish external next from an internal fold with typed break.
Implement co_next, co_flow_next and co_fold without an iterator library, then build an unfused equivalent and compare exact source-pull and callback counts before timing.

Enumerate half-open ranges, nonunit steps, empty take, exhaustion and early break against a materialized mathematical oracle. Check UINT16-edge squaring and resumed iteration; reject extra-pull-after-take and skipped-map mutants.

Replace pure mapping with a callback that acquires resources and may fail. State whether a rejected item was consumed and which resources remain owned; delayed assessment adds zip with unequal lengths and forbids over-reading the shorter input.

subtopics.title: Volcano scan/filter/group operators with pull backpressure

objectives.text: Explain open/next/close and group-boundary ownership in a pull dataflow plan; distinguish iterator backpressure from unbounded eager materialization.
Implement the fused contiguous-key nonnegative-sum query, an unfused scan/filter/group operator chain and a bounded push adapter with identical error and order contracts.

Compare all short key/value streams against an independent grouping oracle, including negative-only groups, overflow, repeated keys separated by another group, early close and output canaries. Reject negative-value inclusion and consuming-later-groups mutants.

Change the source to partial asynchronous batches and the sink to bounded capacity. Preserve one pending group across empty batches and cancellation; delayed assessment adds an ordering operator that cannot remain streaming and requires explicit memory admission.

subtopics.title: Allocated coroutine frames and generator ownership

objectives.text: Derive frame state, suspension lifetime, allocation failure and destruction rules; distinguish compiler-generated C++ coroutine storage from an explicit C frame.

Implement allocator-backed Fibonacci generators with one owned frame, stable DONE, cancellation through destroy and exactly-once release, plus a caller-provided-frame alternative under an equal value contract.

Inject allocation failure, count0/1/47, suspension then destroy, repeated destroy through the cleared owner and interleaved generators. Compare every value with an independent integer recurrence and record allocation counts; reject extra-yield and omitted-release mutants.

Make yielded values own heap buffers and retain one across suspension. Define borrow/transfer/clone explicitly and compare cleanup after partial construction; delayed assessment introduces an address-sensitive self-reference that forbids moving the frame.

subtopics.title: Actual x86-64 stack switching, ABI state and sanitizer fibers

objectives.text: Derive the SysV stack-entry alignment and callee-preserved context, separating ABI obligations, ISO C, compiler extensions and detector annotations.
Implement the assembly context switch plus fresh/resume/yield/completed/destroyed lifecycle on a caller-owned aligned stack; preserve FP control and integrate ASan/TSan fiber APIs.

Run real two-yield callbacks with persistent locals, architectural RSP inside the supplied stack and independent caller/fiber rounding modes. Reject FP-control omission and suspended-destruction mutants. Inspect ELF notes, disassembly, registers, detector results and exact unsupported ABI features.

Add nested fiber scheduling and cooperative cancellation with owned automatic resources. Design guard-page allocation only in an isolated process without host-policy changes, and explain why CET, unwinding, signals and thread migration each require a new backend contract; delayed assessment ports the context layout to another ABI on paper before code.

subtopics.title: Defunctionalized continuations and a budgeted trampoline

objectives.text: Transform recursive factorial into continuation-passing form and then a finite continuation representation, explaining which control and environment values were made explicit.
Implement the factorial0..12 frame with a bounded multiplier stack, one-transition budgets, stable completion and cancellation, without recursive calls or tail-call optimization assumptions.

Compare factorial values with Python integers for every admitted n and every budget partition, including budget0 and cancellation at each state. Assert maximum depth and output publication; reject zero-base and omitted-multiplication mutants.

Replace factorial with a binary expression evaluator whose continuations own temporary buffers. Define tagged continuation cases, overflow/error propagation and cancellation cleanup; delayed assessment introduces an externally supplied continuation that can suspend rather than immediately return.

subtopics.title: Cursor parser combinators with rollback and progress checks

objectives.text: Derive ordered-choice, sequence and repetition semantics over a cursor, distinguishing ordinary mismatch from resource/structural failure and identifying nullable repetition nontermination.
Implement literal/empty/sequence/choice/many on the bounded immutable parser DAG with a node-visit budget, output rollback and no parser library; integrate an explicit bytes.cursor adapter.

Enumerate short strings against an independently written grammar evaluator, including ambiguous prefixes, empty input, exhausted budgets, malformed graph edges and many(empty). Reject committed-choice and nullable-many acceptance mutants.

Add a cut/commit operator and bounded diagnostic expectations. Explain which alternatives can no longer backtrack and how error offsets remain meaningful; delayed assessment changes complete input to segmented input and distinguishes NEED_MORE from NO_MATCH.

subtopics.title: Packrat success and failure memoization with explicit cache identity

objectives.text: Derive the memo key and time/space bound for the fixed ordered-choice grammar; explain why mutable semantic state, input revision and hidden iterative work can invalidate a linear-time claim.
Implement the bounded S grammar with caller-owned success/failure cells, full-input acceptance and per-cell evaluation counts, preserving payload output on mismatch.

Enumerate all short strings over a,b,c,x against a direct language-shape recognizer, then test deep c-ending branches that revisit the same inner S. Assert at most n+1 cell evaluations and exact endpoints; reject omitted memo lookup and wrong cached endpoint mutants.

Add a stateful symbol predicate or an input edit and derive the necessary cache invalidation/key expansion. Then add direct left recursion and show why the current recursion algorithm does not become safe merely by setting an in-progress bit; delayed assessment designs a bounded left-recursion policy.

subtopics.title: Readiness-based async frames and the register/recheck race

objectives.text: Explain readiness as a hint, partial progress as frame state, and registration/quiescence lifetime; distinguish this model from completion submission rings and automatic Rust Future pinning.

Implement exact-length asynchronous reads with at most two reads per poll, arm-then-recheck, generation-scoped notifications, synchronous disarm and cancelled/error terminal states. Build an io.reactor/io.stream/io.deadline adapter.

Script readiness arriving between the first AGAIN and arm, repeated spurious wakeups, short progress plus ERROR, EOF, stale notifications and cancel. Preserve final output until complete and count all callbacks; reject omitted recheck and omitted disarm mutants.

Move notification delivery to another thread and make disarm asynchronous. Introduce a separate quiescence acknowledgment and retained frame ownership, then test all cancellation/completion orders; delayed assessment replaces a borrowed read buffer with a copied channel message.

subtopics.title: Single-shot resumable effects with explicit continuation ownership

objectives.text: Derive a two-question effect program and its defunctionalized continuation environment, separating single-shot runtime tokens from effect typing and multi-shot control capture.
Implement start/resume/abort with owner+generation tokens, checked second-answer addition, consumed continuation handles and unchanged state on arithmetic rejection.

Enumerate answer pairs and replay every stale token while the frame is live; test overflow followed by a valid retry, abort and completed reuse. Reject replay-admission and dropped-first-answer mutants; record synthetic duplicate-result attempts as bounded property violations.

Nest two handlers with different question policies and add a resource owned across a suspension. Specify lexical/dynamic handler lookup and abort cleanup; delayed assessment asks for multi-shot continuation cloning and requires an explicit clone policy instead of copying owned pointers.

domains.title: Structured concurrency, channels and actors
domains.depth: Mechanism construction, falsification, composition and independent transfer

subtopics.title: Scope-owned child tasks and cooperative cancellation

objectives.text: Explain scope-owned task lifetime, failure aggregation and cooperative cancellation, including why a cancellation flag does not establish completion or a bounded join latency.

Derive admission/closing/quiescent states, implement spawn/join and deterministic error selection, then compose with the existing work.pool artifact without detached tasks or prematurely released contexts.

Inject failure before every admission, record thread/context ownership, join zero/one/eight children, reject ninth admission and late spawn. Use a barrier-controlled failure with siblings acknowledging cancellation and compare accepted/completed counts. Reject both missing-cancellation and swallowed-result mutants. Run separate TSan and demonstrate that eventual cancellation needs child checkpoints.

Add nested nurseries with a parent deadline: propagate cancellation down while joining upward, retaining contexts until every descendant is quiescent. Delayed assessment supplies two failures racing in different orders; keep deterministic creation-order reporting while preserving both errors in a bounded aggregate.

subtopics.title: Bounded CSP channels, rendezvous and atomic select

objectives.text: Derive readiness, linearization, close/drain and cancellation semantics; compare deterministic selection with Go ready-case randomness and distinguish rendezvous acknowledgment from merely enqueuing an offer.

Implement buffered/rendezvous operations and select with a single predicate-registration boundary, explicit spurious-wakeup loops, finite tickets and quiescent destruction; retain coroutine frames until generation-specific disarm.

Test full/empty, both ready, one closed, all closed, close with buffered values, cancellation with blocked sender/receiver and accepted-versus-unaccepted rendezvous. Repeatedly inject spurious broadcasts. Capture event histories and verify no lost/duplicated accepted values. Reject send-after-close and skipped-buffer mutants; independently model sequential traces and use TSan for actual threads.

Change unsigned copies to owned buffers with a destructor: define ownership on failed send, close/drain and cancellation. Delayed assessment splits the hub into separately locked channels; derive a registration/recheck protocol that prevents a wakeup lost between observing empty and going to sleep, or justify retaining the common lock.

subtopics.title: Senders, receivers and immovable operation-state lifetimes

objectives.text: Separate sender recipe, connected operation storage, start permission and completion ownership; identify the dated C++ proposal guarantees that an exposed C struct does not enforce.
Implement the serialized state protocol and backend lifetime adapter, including synchronous completion, cancellation races, callback reentrancy policy and exactly-once terminal release.

Enumerate invalid start/complete orders, value/error/stopped alternatives and cancellation-before-completion. Use a receiver that frees a heap state to detect post-callback access under ASan. Reject duplicate-completion and cancel-as-completion mutants. For a concurrent adapter, use one atomic winner and demonstrate that losers never inspect reclaimed storage without their own retained reference.

Allow an operation to complete inline during start and let the receiver destroy its enclosing object. Delayed assessment connects a chain of two operations; ensure the successor starts only after ownership transfers and no predecessor field is accessed after its receiver may have destroyed it.

subtopics.title: Actor incarnations, copied mailboxes and failure boundaries

objectives.text: Explain mailbox ownership, actor identity across restart, run-to-completion serialization and the limit of let-it-crash recovery when effects have already escaped the actor.
Implement admission, dispatch, death and reincarnation with finite generation retirement; design the channel-to-actor executor boundary and message-drop ownership.

Test full mailbox, stale identity, nested step, failure with queued work, restart while alive and generation exhaustion. Reject stale-generation admission and retained-dead-mailbox mutants. Record effects before failure to show they are not rolled back. Compare actor serialization to a mutex-protected shared object under the same observable ordering.

Messages become owned buffers and handlers may enqueue to themselves: implement deterministic destruction of abandoned messages without recursive dispatch. Delayed assessment receives a late reply addressed to a previous incarnation after restart; route it to an explicit dead-letter sink and prevent delivery to the replacement actor.

subtopics.title: Supervision trees with restart budgets and ordered quiescence

objectives.text: Derive restart topology, intensity accounting and the error-kernel boundary; explain why restarting healthy siblings may be necessary and why unlimited restart can amplify faults.
Implement ordered restart plans with bounded timestamp storage and an actor execution adapter that preserves quiescence and accounts for partial restart failure.

Independently enumerate all12 strategy/failed-child selections, test exact window boundary, backwards time, maximum timestamps and escalation permanence. Reject forward-stop and omitted-start mutants. Inject handler and restart failures, compare emitted action order and prove no restarted child observes a dependency that is still stopped.

Replace the flat four-child group with a two-level tree and distinct parent/child budgets. Delayed assessment makes child2 depend on child1 initialization and fail during restart; derive whether to escalate, roll back already restarted children or retain a documented degraded state.

subtopics.title: Bounded work stealing with an explicit C memory-order proof

objectives.text: Identify linearization and ownership in owner/thief races, last-item arbitration, finite-index exhaustion and stale slot reads; distinguish SC correctness from weak-order proof and actual lock-free progress.
Derive a circular representation with monotonic nonwrapping indices and atomic slots; implement push/pop/steal with a proof for empty, full, last-item and reused-slot states.

Differentially compare1095 bounded sequential traces with Python deque, include repeated empty pops and capacity reuse, record concurrent invocation/response histories and check small histories for legal linearizations. Reject wrong-pop and omitted-steal-CAS mutants. Run TSan, inspect generated instructions and report atomic_is_lock_free; do not infer weak-memory correctness from x86 stress.

Weaken SC to acquire/release/fences one edge at a time, deriving a C memory-model argument and model-checker counterexamples before benchmarking. Delayed assessment changes payloads to pointers and permits array growth: add a reclamation scheme and prove a losing thief cannot dereference freed storage.

subtopics.title: TL2-style software transactions over actual C17 atomics

objectives.text: Derive snapshot validation, write-set locking, abort restoration and the distinction between transaction isolation, atomic C accesses and memory reclamation; explain inconsistent-read hazards before commit.

Implement bounded read/write sets, read-your-writes, nonblocking lock acquisition and validated commit using the declared SC baseline; prove failed commits leave payload unchanged while allowing timestamp gaps.

Force conflict before a read, after a read and during partial lock acquisition; test repeated writes, empty/read-only transactions and timestamp exhaustion. Reject missing read validation and missing commit validation mutants. Use an independent serial-history model for small schedules, TSan for actual threads and fault hooks for every commit phase. Explain why atomic individual loads alone do not provide a coherent transaction.

Introduce a retryable callback with a synthetic log effect: stage it for commit or supply compensation rather than replaying it blindly. Delayed assessment allows dynamically allocated nodes and privatization; show why the fixed-cell proof says nothing about reclaimed node lifetime and design a compatible reclamation protocol.

subtopics.title: Multiversion visibility, reader pins and bounded reclamation

objectives.text: Derive version visibility and retention from reader lifetimes, distinguish repeatable snapshot reads from stronger isolation, and identify how a forgotten pin creates resource retention.
Implement timestamped publication, exact pin identity, visible-version selection and reclamation with a bounded-space proof under the four-reader assumption.

Enumerate pin/publish/read/drop traces against an independent immutable-history model, test four pins at different versions and a fifth refusal, stale slot reuse and generation retirement. Reject pin-ignorant collection and missing-generation mutants. Track retained version counts before/after releases and compare the mutex cost with read-copy-update assumptions.

Give each version separately owned payload storage whose clone can fail; publish only after full construction and preserve old readers on failure. Delayed assessment adds independent keys and predicate queries: construct write skew under snapshot isolation and explain what validation or locking would establish the stronger requested property.

subtopics.title: Sequence validation without racing ordinary C payloads

objectives.text: Separate storage race freedom, coherent snapshot validation, writer serialization, retry bounds and counter lifetime; identify what SC proves and what a later weakened implementation must re-establish.
Derive the atomic representation and SC ordering argument, implement bounded retry and nonwrapping writer publication, and account for every output and failure effect.

Test odd/even transitions, zero retry, interrupted writer state, output canaries and counter exhaustion. Reject odd-sequence acceptance and omitted-payload-write mutants. Run actual concurrent stress and TSan while explaining that clean runs do not prove weak-order correctness. Inspect disassembly and compare lock-free status and fences with an equivalent mutex snapshot.

Derive a weaker-order version from explicit synchronization/fence reasoning and check it with a C memory-model tool before comparing costs. Delayed assessment uses pointer payloads and a reader that pauses after loading one pointer; add lifetime protection or reject the design, since sequence validation does not retain pointees.

subtopics.title: Demand signaling, terminal events and bounded reentrancy

objectives.text: Derive demand accounting, signal ordering, cancellation and reentrancy limits; compare the original C subset to selected Reactive Streams rules without claiming interface or certification equivalence.
Implement explicit demand/terminal/delivering state, saturating unbounded arithmetic and callback ownership; construct a channel adapter that never delivers more items than requested.

Enumerate request/emit/cancel/end traces, test zero and maximum demand, callback requests/cancellation and recursive emission. Reject emission without credit and repeated-terminal mutants. Independently account for requested versus delivered finite items, retain callback context through return and test that end requires no demand.

Make signals originate on several threads: serialize them through one executor and retain the subscription until all in-flight signals quiesce. Delayed assessment introduces a slow subscriber and bounded channel capacity; compare blocking, dropping and failure policies under the same stated delivery contract, with T75 owning the overload decision.

domains.title: Managed-runtime object models
domains.depth: Mechanism construction, experimental falsification and independent transfer

subtopics.title: Pointer tags, NaN payloads and representation trust boundaries

objectives.text: Derive disjoint number and integer bit partitions, pointer round-trip preconditions and negative decoding; classify portable arithmetic, implementation-defined pointer mapping and explicit IEEE-format assumptions.

Implement numeric NaN canonicalization, int32 boxing/unboxing and checked two-bit pointer tags from the exact contract. Build a discriminated-union alternative and a character-copy double bridge with verified format assumptions; never truncate a pointer into a payload.

Enumerate signed extrema and NaN payload collisions, signed zero, infinities, misaligned integer mappings and reserved bits. Reject missing-canonicalization and sign-loss mutants; compare integer decoding with Python integers and verify native pointer round trips only for admitted live objects.

Change to a capability-pointer target or a binary32-only implementation: derive an explicit handle representation and revise every pointer/NaN assumption. Delayed assessment introduces a serialized attacker-controlled NaN word; demonstrate why decoding it cannot authorize a host pointer.

subtopics.title: Owned binary interning and collision-safe symbol identity

objectives.text: Explain canonical identity versus byte equality, table ownership, embedded-NUL handling and why collisions cannot prove equality. Distinguish strong intern retention from weak symbol tables.
