Implement the eight-entry copied-string table with first-insertion IDs and atomic admission failure, then implement a hashed table with explicit collision chains or probing and transactional resizing; compare both on the same byte-string contract.

Generate binary strings including empty, embedded NUL and equal-length different bytes. Inject failure on hits and misses, exhaust capacity and preserve output/state snapshots. Reject length-only equality and ignored-admission-failure mutants; use a Python dictionary as an independent identity oracle.

Replace strong retention with weak interning linked to collector epochs, defining when IDs retire and whether reinterned bytes regain the same identity. Delayed assessment retains a symbol across a moving collection and forces an allocation failure during rehash.

subtopics.title: Immutable hidden classes and reusable property transitions

objectives.text: Derive ordered layout descriptors and transition identity, distinguishing an equal property set from an equal storage layout. State ownership of shapes, receiver fields and transition caches.

Implement immutable four-field shapes in a16-shape arena, transition reuse by parent-plus-key and atomic capacity failure. Add a dictionary-mode alternative for deletion and compare its explicit lookup/invalidation contract.

Construct same-order and permuted-order receivers, update existing properties at full capacity, exhaust transition storage and test rollback. Reject parent-omission and omitted-receiver-transition mutants; independently compare every lookup with a property dictionary.

Add property deletion, attributes and a prototype chain. Derive which operations preserve shape identity and which invalidate caches. Delayed assessment permits shape ID reuse and requires a generation or epoch policy that rejects stale descriptors.

subtopics.title: Monomorphic and polymorphic inline-cache guards

objectives.text: Explain a cached lookup handler versus a cached value, and prove why owner, shape and property key jointly determine this model offset. Bound the cases in which immutable shapes remove invalidation needs.

Implement a two-entry polymorphic cache with monomorphic first state, sticky generic fallback, owner reset and current-receiver field loads. Compare always-generic lookup with the same output and missing-key effects.

Alternate receivers with different insertion orders and property names at one cache, update field values, switch arenas and test missing outputs. Reject missing-shape and missing-key guards; count hits/misses before timing equivalent workloads.

Add prototype-chain access or shape retirement with weak cache references, then design invalidation tokens and deoptimization fallback. Delayed assessment inserts an accessor whose callback mutates the receiver during lookup.

subtopics.title: Incremental marking and root/store write barriers

objectives.text: Derive the no-black-to-white-edge invariant and distinguish incremental mutation between steps from concurrent mutation. Explain floating garbage and why root updates need their own barrier.

Implement begin, bounded scan steps, black-source stores and root insertion for the16-object graph. Build an explicit gray-worklist alternative with a capacity proof, and add immediate quiescent sweeping under a stated allocation policy.

Enumerate small graphs/root sets against graph reachability; stop after blackening a root, then insert a white child and add a new white root. Reject missing-object and missing-root barriers, test budget0, cycles and invalid edges, and account for scan work separately from elapsed time.

Permit allocation during an active cycle and compare black allocation, gray allocation and a restart policy. Delayed assessment replaces serialized mutation with a concurrent mutator; derive publication ordering and termination detection rather than adding volatile.

subtopics.title: Semispace evacuation, forwarding and promotion failure

objectives.text: Derive identity preservation under copying, forwarding uniqueness and the old-to-young root obligation. Explain the empirical generational hypothesis separately from the correctness of a minor collection.

Implement two young semispaces with first-survival aging, second-survival promotion, complete root/edge rewriting and atomic capacity failure. Replace the whole-state transaction copy with a preflight or rollback design while retaining the same failure contract.

Compare surviving payload identities and edge relations against graph reachability over all small graphs. Test cycles, aliases, old-only roots, two successive collections and promotion exhaustion. Reject skipped-old-roots and stale-root-rewrite mutants, measuring copied survivors rather than claiming every allocation is cheap.

Integrate card scanning and a major collector; choose a promotion policy under an adversarial long-lived workload and bounded old capacity. Delayed assessment adds large nonmovable objects and requires a precise pinning/fragmentation policy.

subtopics.title: Card marking and conservative remembered roots

objectives.text: Derive old-to-young completeness and distinguish safe false positives from unsafe false negatives. Explain why overwriting one field cannot clear a card shared by another field.

Implement two-object cards over eight old objects, store marking and dirty-card rescanning with retained young edges. Integrate it with the nursery through an explicit adapter, retaining full-old scanning as an independent reference.

Enumerate object/field/target stores, test two young edges sharing a card, overwrite one and then both, and count exactly four field scans per dirty card. Reject omitted marking and premature clearing mutants; compare survivor graphs with the full-scan nursery.

Add concurrent card scanning with a writer racing card clearing and design an epoch/double-buffer or synchronization protocol. Delayed assessment changes card size and cache-line placement; revise false-positive work and cache traffic measurements.

subtopics.title: Handle-based compaction and forwarding aliases

objectives.text: Distinguish object identity, handle identity and physical slot, and derive when outstanding raw borrows prohibit movement. Explain forwarding for aliased handles and nested handle fields.

Implement stable physical packing of live payloads with old-slot forwarding and updating every handle alias, then add a pinned-object alternative with explicit fragmentation costs and a generation policy for reused handles.

Enumerate all small live masks and compare payload identity through handles before and after movement. Test holes, aliases, cycles through handles, empty/full heaps, and borrow rejection; reject omitted-handle-rewrite and ignored-borrow mutants.

Integrate a pool allocator and a foreign-function API that temporarily exposes raw pointers. Design pin/unpin lifetime and cancellation cleanup, and measure the tradeoff against copying handles. Delayed assessment allows handle-slot reuse with a stale external reference.

subtopics.title: Ephemeron fixed points and staged finalization

objectives.text: Derive conditional reachability of ephemeron values and why a value-to-key cycle cannot bootstrap liveness. Separate weak clearing, finalizer retention, resurrection and deterministic external-resource release.

Implement repeated ephemeron closure, weak clearing before finalizer retention, an explicit pending queue and at-most-once finalization identities. Build a synthetic finalizer driver that may resurrect an object and compare the chosen policy with Lua and CPython.

Enumerate small ephemeron relations/root sets independently, include reverse-ordered chains requiring multiple passes, value-key cycles, weak-only roots, pending-queue rejection and resurrection followed by later reclamation. Reject single-pass and missing-finalized-bit mutants.

Add a finalizer that fails while owning a synthetic resource and one that allocates; specify queue capacity, reentry and eventual cleanup without relying on prompt GC. Delayed assessment changes ephemeron values into graphs containing further ephemeron keys.

subtopics.title: Trial deletion for reference-counted cycles

objectives.text: Derive residual external counts for a candidate subgraph, then prove why residual zero alone does not imply garbage. Preserve true counts while detecting a candidate reachability closure.

Implement copied trial counts, candidate-internal edge subtraction, rescue from positive residual seeds, and reclamation with decrements to surviving targets. Integrate ordinary zero-count cascading separately and compare with a tracing oracle.

Enumerate three-node graphs, external roots and candidate subsets, including self-cycles, shared descendants, parallel edges, externally protected cycles and inconsistent counts. Reject omitted subtraction and missing rescue closure; verify true survivor counts and exact reclaimed sets.

Add deferred decrements and candidate buffering, bounding pause and memory cost under repeated mutations. Delayed assessment introduces concurrent retain/release and asks which snapshots and synchronization are needed before a trial result can justify reclamation.

subtopics.title: Precise root maps and derived-reference relocation

objectives.text: Derive complete root maps over initialized interpreter slots, distinguishing scalar lookalikes, duplicate copies and derived base-plus-offset references. Explain compiler statepoints versus manually maintained C roots.

Implement transactional map validation and relocation of every root copy, preserving scalar slots and one-past offsets. Integrate actual runtime.vm roots and temporaries through ADAPTERS.md, then construct and inspect an LLVM statepoint experiment as a separate compiler-dependent artifact.

Enumerate base/destination/offset combinations, exact maps, missing roots, uninitialized slots, missing forwarding and non-safepoint rejection. Reject omitted-map-validation and omitted-relocation mutants; inspect pre/post values and demonstrate why stale hidden compiler copies require compiler cooperation.

Add multiple interpreter frames, exceptions and foreign calls that can allocate. Design root registration/unregistration on every exit and safepoint poll protocol. Delayed assessment moves an object while two derived references and a scalar with equal bits are live.

domains.title: Flow control and resilient services
domains.depth: Implementation, failure investigation, resource accounting and independent transfer

subtopics.title: Cancellation trees and budgets across clock domains

objectives.text: Derive deadline versus timeout semantics, cancellation precedence, parent lifetime and nonextension of inherited budget. Distinguish stopping admission from acknowledgement and rollback.

Implement checked scope construction and cross-clock remaining-budget encoding, including zero budget, numeric horizon, depth exhaustion and stale parent-lifetime counterexamples without executing invalid access.

Enumerate cancellation/expiry/finish orderings and verify output preservation, no later child deadline, idempotent cancellation and delayed borrower cleanup. Inject a completion after cancellation and retain its state until acknowledgement.

Transfer to an RPC chain with queued transport delay and independent clocks. Quantify which latency assumptions bound end-to-end completion and show why repeated per-hop timeout resets or copying an absolute monotonic timestamp violate the intended budget.

subtopics.title: Five overload policies and bounded pending producers

objectives.text: Specify each policy in terms of observable loss, ordering, caller ownership and completion; distinguish application admission, transport buffering and receiver consumption.
Implement all five policies, closed draining and the real channel adapter, including exactly-once transfer and explicit retained pending state.

Implement a two-producer readiness/cancellation adapter and falsify missed-wakeup, double-transfer and unbounded-pending assumptions with controlled event traces; bound queue plus producer-held memory together. Add explicit credit messages: start with four credits, consume one on admission, return one only when receiver capacity is released, and reject duplicate/stale credit returns so granted minus consumed plus returned never exceeds actual capacity.

Compare block/reject/drop/overwrite/degrade under an identical synthetic producer/consumer schedule, measuring accepted, lost, coalesced, queued and pending work separately. Transfer to owned payloads with a disposer and prove exactly-once cleanup on every rejected or discarded path.

subtopics.title: Hashed timer-wheel collisions, cancellation and expiry work

objectives.text: Derive bucket index, full due identity, list invariants and generation retirement. Prove why modulo bucket equality alone is insufficient across revolutions.
Implement bounded schedule/cancel/tick and a two-level cascade extension with no lost or duplicate expiries, explicit horizon, late tick and immediate timer policies.
Enumerate delays1..16, cancellation/reuse traces and same-bucket collisions against an ordered due-event oracle; test numeric exhaustion and every link removal position.

Compare heap, ordered list and wheel using equivalent ordering, horizon and cancellation guarantees. Measure worst expiry burst, empty-tick work, memory and jitter; distinguish per-timer output cost from constant bookkeeping claims.

subtopics.title: Overflow-safe token buckets and competing rate contracts

objectives.text: Derive the burst-plus-rate admission bound, initial credit, dimensional units and distinction between a policer, shaper, peak limit and concurrency limit.
Implement overflow-safe lazy refill and fixed-point fractional credit, specifying rounding, numeric horizon and which state changes persist on a rejected spend.

Exhaust small capacities/rates/time jumps against arbitrary-precision arithmetic and adversarial boundary costs; verify cumulative admitted cost bounds and kill free-refill/equality-rejection mutants.

Compose average and peak limits with atomic admission across both budgets. Compare token bucket and fixed/sliding windows under the same burst policy, and identify when different results arise from different contracts rather than implementation quality.

subtopics.title: Jittered retry schedules with a shared deadline and attempt budget

objectives.text: Derive bounded exponential windows, count the original attempt separately and explain why nested retries multiply work. Classify retryable outcomes without treating timeout as absence of side effects.
Implement schedule, unbiased bounded PRNG adapter and actual fault-model dispatch with a common limiter, preserving ownership of outstanding attempts until completion.
Enumerate every allowed draw for windows2/4/8, deadlines at each boundary and all capped attempt histories; use fault traces where an effect commits but its acknowledgement is lost.

Compare no-jitter, full-jitter and a documented alternative under fixed seeds and equal retry/deadline budgets. Measure peak synchronized work as well as completion latency; transfer to correlated client seeds and expose why jitter is not a security or safety guarantee.

subtopics.title: Health breakers, bulkheads and stale completions

objectives.text: Derive distinct health and capacity invariants, permit ownership, epoch identity and neutral-versus-backend-failure classification; explain why a failure window is not a concurrency bound.
Implement bounded admission/completion with generation and epoch exhaustion, including late old-epoch results and four-tick cooldown overflow retirement.
Model every two-permit completion ordering, stale/duplicate completion and half-open race. Add and test a sliding-window policy with an independent recomputation of its retained observations.

Transfer to two tenants and heterogeneous request costs. Derive isolation guarantees, starvation tradeoffs and cancellation acknowledgement, then compare recovery latency and retained resources under equal admission policies.

subtopics.title: Hedged responses and ownership of losing work

objectives.text: Separate first response from first acceptable response, result commitment from quiescence, and cancellation request from completed losing work. State prerequisites for safe hedging of side effects.
Implement exactly one winner and separately owned attempt lifetimes, with expiry, late response, repeated completion and unstarted-attempt rejection.

Implement and verify a synchronized two-worker completion arbiter, exercising both simultaneous success orders and winner/cancellation/timeout races under a controlled scheduler plus sanitizer checks.

Measure tail latency and total backend work under explicit independent versus correlated delay models. Transfer to a slow loser that completes after the client abandons its wait; preserve cleanup and prevent a stale generation from completing a new request.

subtopics.title: Idempotent effects, finite deduplication and storage fencing

objectives.text: Derive request identity versus payload equality, finite retention, authentication assumption and monotonic fencing enforcement at the actual effect resource. Identify which failures make a result uncertain.
Implement atomic in-memory record/effect publication, original-response replay, parameter mismatch rejection, no live-record eviction and checked arithmetic.

Demonstrate harmless replay/stale-writer violations using original mutants, then add a journal recovery model with crash injection at every write/flush/commit boundary and independently recompute recovered effects.

Transfer to multiple clients, reordered messages, restarted token issuer and expired dedup entries. State durability, uniqueness and monotonicity assumptions necessary for each guarantee; reject claims of network exactly-once delivery from a local lookup table.

subtopics.title: Resilient telemetry admission, committed effects and draining

objectives.text: Derive a composition contract with admission, effect commit, reply availability, notification enqueue, delivery and cleanup as distinct events. Account for every retained buffer, timer, permit and borrowed owner.

Implement the bounded service anchor using actual conc.channel and all required local IPC/reactor/fault adapters; preserve exactly-once notification for a new retained request and explicit replay/expiry semantics.

Inject allocation/partial-I/O/timeout/reset/cancellation/late-completion faults across the integrated service, checking effect and notification accounting with an independent event-sourced oracle and all declared capacity bounds.

Run an independently designed workload with burst arrivals, long tails, correlated faults and slow consumers. Seal a composition decision, apply all13 cost dimensions, and explain changed results under different correctness contracts or clock assumptions.

domains.title: Replicated state, event history and deterministic replay
domains.depth: Mechanism construction, falsification, composition and independent transfer

subtopics.title: Positioned event logs and persistent snapshot roots

objectives.text: Distinguish immutable event history, a current projection, a retained snapshot root and durable storage. Derive why replay requires event-version and external-query assumptions, not merely a list of bytes.

Retain the actual PR-T70-07 learner artifact and its64node/3nodes-per-update contract. Prove16 appends use48nodes, every published root remains immutable and an interrupted failed append cannot advance count. Initialization requires no surviving borrowed roots; do not copy/relocate a live arena and interpret roots in another owner. Account for unpublished cells and allocation counters separately from reachable state. State a release/publication order for a future concurrent adapter.

Run replicated.log and the three allocation-cut assertions, compare every prefix against an independent key/value dictionary and rebuild into a fresh arena. Reject count-before-commit and latest-root-for-all-snapshots mutants. Inspect source/link dependencies to establish that the real imported HAMT is used. Separately implement the required codec.records/storage.pages adapter with short writes and crash schedules; the memory anchor does not validate that adapter.

Replace the in-memory append with versioned checksummed records on the prior storage.pages artifact; enumerate every tear/flush prefix and recover the longest committed prefix. Persist snapshots with their event position and schema identity. Demonstrate why replaying an external effect twice or using a changed external query result changes semantics; retain original responses as events where required.

subtopics.title: CQRS projection admission and atomic position advancement

objectives.text: Separate query-model choice from delivery semantics. Establish exactly-once application only within one serialized projection and one retained immutable log identity; reject the stronger claim of exactly-once external effects.

Prove the invariant count=k implies exactly the first k events contributed once and applied[i].position=i+1. A 16-term int32 sum fits int64 on the declared target. Retain history for conflict checks rather than trusting a reused position from a new log. The caller must associate a projection with one log identity. Explain why a mutex around cursor alone is insufficient, and why an external email/file effect cannot become atomic with this state by naming it CQRS.

Run replicated.projection, including actual pthread schedules under GCC TSan when available. Kill duplicate-reapplication and gap-acceptance mutants with semantic assertions. Record mutex boundaries and model the crash point between query-state and cursor persistence. A TSan pass observes these executions only; it does not certify arbitrary effects or all schedules.

Add a durable inbox/outbox with log UUID and idempotency keys using storage.pages and ipc.local. Enumerate crash/retry points on both sides of a local synthetic receiver. Produce one duplicate-side-effect counterexample without receiver deduplication and show the residual requirement for atomic receiver state. Compare rebuildable read models with authoritative event history.

subtopics.title: Lamport, vector and hybrid logical clock boundaries

objectives.text: Derive three different clock contracts: Lamport timestamps preserve happened-before in one direction, vectors characterize causality under fixed known membership, and HLC pairs retain a physical component without eliminating physical-clock assumptions.

Show two concurrent events with ordered Lamport timestamps, two incomparable vectors and every HLC equality case. Separate physical-clock closeness claims from the synchronization assumptions in Corollary1. On local overflow choose explicit failure; neither arbitrary sleep nor silently increasing physical time is equivalent. Outputs are ordinary C structs, so validity and per-replica serialization remain caller obligations.

Run replicated.clocks and independent exhaustive small HLC branch enumeration plus uint64/uint32 extrema. Kill ignoring-remote Lamport and incorrect equal-physical HLC-counter mutants. Build small message histories and derive causal relations from graph reachability before comparing clock outputs; timestamp ordering alone is not the oracle.

Change replica membership and persisted restart identities; show why resetting a vector slot or reusing a timestamp identity loses history. Add a bounded clock-skew model and prove exactly which HLC closeness bound follows. Compare scalar timestamp wire size, vector growth, and a protocol that waits versus rejects on finite counter exhaustion.

subtopics.title: Join-semilattice counters and deterministic registers

objectives.text: Derive convergence from explicit componentwise joins and globally unique writer identities, and distinguish state merge from replaying operations. A last-writer register resolves an order chosen by the protocol, not necessarily real-time recency.

Prove idempotence, commutativity and associativity on admitted compatible states, plus inflation of each grow-only component. Explain why sum of received states double-counts retransmission, why finite overflow must reject, and why a reused writer identity with forked state violates the ownership model. For registers identify conflict cases outside the unique-event assumption and the total-order tie rule.

Run replicated.counters; enumerate small component states and three-way merge permutations, including duplicate, reordered and dropped-then-retransmitted messages. Kill additive-state-merge and missing replica tie-break mutants. Show a counterexample for unchecked uint32 wrap and for independent writers sharing one replica slot.

Add membership replacement, serialized snapshots and state corruption detection. Distinguish crash fault tolerance from Byzantine tolerance: demonstrate a synthetic forged high component monopolizing the merge and specify an authenticated admission/identity policy without claiming signatures solve semantic authorization. Compare state size with operation-log retention under the same delivery assumptions.

subtopics.title: Observed-remove sets and replayable delta state

objectives.text: Explain add-wins observed removal through unique add identities, retained tombstones and idempotent delta joins. Distinguish a causally self-contained delta representation from arbitrary partial operations or unsafe tombstone collection.

Define membership as adds minus removed. Derive why a concurrent unobserved add survives removal and why an observed add cannot resurrect when its delta arrives again. Treat one writer per replica as a premise. The bounded delta carries exact tag tombstones, so remove-before-add delivery is representable; do not infer this for all causal CRDTs. Explain the delta-interval causal precondition from the paper and specify acknowledgment/stability requirements before reclaiming history.

Run replicated.sets and enumerate two-writer add/remove/delivery traces against a mathematical tagged-set oracle. Include duplicate and remove-before-add delivery. Kill remove-all-possible-tags and omitted-tombstone-merge mutants. Inventory retained tags and show the exact full condition rather than silently dropping history.

Introduce a third replica, disconnection and crash/restart. Design a causal delta-interval anti-entropy protocol with durable incarnation/counter identity and full-state fallback; falsify premature garbage collection with a delayed old delta. Prove a stable frontier before discarding tombstones, or retain them and quantify growth.

subtopics.title: Replicated sequence identities and contextual transformation

objectives.text: Separate stable sequence identity from transient visible position, and compare a bounded parent-tree sequence with context-dependent operational transformation. Pairwise insertion agreement is a necessary local property, not a complete OT correctness theorem.

Derive acyclicity from parent<id and closure from causal admission. Prove insertion-order-independent rendering for a fixed admitted node set, including descendants of deleted anchors. Explain that this original tree contract is RGA-inspired, not a claim to implement every detail of Specification19. For OT derive the two-branch diamond under distinct priorities and identify the state-vector/log context needed beyond it.

Run replicated.sequence; enumerate topological arrival orders and deletion subsets against a recursive tree oracle. Kill arrival-order sibling rendering and deleted-subtree omission mutants. Check full capacity, duplicate identity, missing dependency and output failure atomicity. Enumerate both paths of the two-insert OT diamond, then provide a three-operation context counterexample to an unjustified generalization.

Add delete operations delivered before insert, Unicode scalar payloads and snapshot compaction. Compare an explicit pending-dependency queue with tombstone admission. Implement an OT context-control protocol with state vectors and retained transformations, identify assumptions about fixed membership and failures, and test more than pairwise transformation equations.

subtopics.title: Merkle commitments and bounded anti-entropy

objectives.text: Derive a domain-separated Merkle root for an exact ordered leaf sequence, distinguishing hash equality under a collision assumption from identity authentication, availability or a proof that arbitrary bytes are well formed.

Derive padding across55/56/63/64/65-byte boundaries, uint32 modular arithmetic, round constants and endian conversion. Prove the tree shape for non-power-of-two counts and that a subtree comparison is meaningful only with the same position/range/domain. Account for hash collision and corrupt-peer assumptions; a matching root alone authenticates no sender and guarantees no retrievability.

Run replicated.merkle, standard empty/abc hash vectors, all padding boundaries and independent randomized hashlib differential cases. Kill omitted leaf-domain prefix and ignored right-child mutants. Inspect the generated code for the intended unsigned operations; benchmark nodes hashed versus full leaf comparison under equal correctness/security contracts.

Add inclusion proofs with explicit leaf index/count, verify malformed/truncated/extra paths, then implement anti-entropy over a synthetic local framed transport. Vary chunking and domain identifiers and show root incompatibility. Model a malicious peer returning a missing or inconsistent node; fail without publishing partial repaired state. Do not claim collision resistance from a finite test suite.

subtopics.title: Field tags, minimal varints and canonical bytes

objectives.text: Distinguish a wire grammar from one canonical encoding and show why deterministic serialization under one binary is not a universal content identity. Derive portable signed ZigZag arithmetic without signed-left-shift assumptions.

For five-byte uint32 varints require the final payload<=15 and no continuation. Derive ZigZag using unsigned conversion/shift and a sign mask; decode odd values as -(value>>1)-1 to include INT32_MIN safely. Prove canonical decode/reencode idempotence and uniqueness for the admitted semantic map. Explain the tradeoff of rejecting duplicate fields compared with protocols that merge repeated occurrences.

Run replicated.wire and an independent Python parser/encoder for boundary values and reordered field maps. Kill overlong-varint acceptance and incorrect negative ZigZag mutants. Enumerate every truncation, duplicate field, forbidden tag/wire type and output-capacity boundary; demonstrate two noncanonical orders producing the same canonical bytes.

Add length-delimited nested records with depth and total-byte budgets, a critical/advisory negotiation rule and an incremental io.frame decoder. Compare schema migration that retains unknown fields against field-wise reconstruction that loses them. Define canonical NaN/negative-zero/string normalization policy before adding floating or textual values; do not assume the current integer proof extends.

subtopics.title: Pure reducers, explicit effects and rollback replay

objectives.text: Implement the T20.03 functional-core boundary: explicit state and recorded input produce new state and effect requests, while an adapter owns effects. Demonstrate rollback equivalence without replaying externally visible effects or claiming that ordinary C enforces purity.

Prove determinism from complete state/input and defined unsigned arithmetic. Identify every effect boundary and distinguish speculative requests from committed presentation. Derive rollback of the HAMT used cursor after a failed second update while preserving old reachable roots; staged unreachable arena cells and allocation counters may differ. All arena users must be quiescent during the transaction, and roots from unpublished intermediate updates must never escape. Score overflow or invalid movement must not partially publish a state/effect.

Run replicated.replay and exhaustively compare all movement histories of length0..8 with a Python integer model; verify suffix rollback versus full replay. Kill omitted random-score contribution and failed second-update allocation-leak mutants. Build a synthetic effect adapter with idempotency key(timeline,tick) and injected failure; record one duplicate-effect counterexample if replay directly invokes the adapter. Inspect undefined symbols to confirm the core has no time/random/I/O dependency.

Introduce two local simulated players, predicted remote inputs and delayed corrections using ipc.local/io.frame, with bounded rollback horizon and retained snapshots. Separate authoritative committed effects from speculative presentation and define replacement/cancellation semantics. Reuse the actual T20.03 learner reducer adapter and storage.pages snapshot backend, then vary compiler/endianness and compare canonical state hashes. Implement a hidden wall-clock/random dependency as a deliberately failing counterexample, not a production change.
